examens.intro:
The Claude certification for business users: framing a task well, judging and checking answers, choosing the right capability (Projects, Artifacts, Skills, Research, code-based analysis, connectors, memory), designing reusable workflows, and using Claude responsibly with company data.

Outline from **guide version 1.1, effective December 7, 2026**: 70 questions (60 scored, 10 unscored), 120 minutes, multiple-choice scenarios, pass mark **720** on 100–1000, USD 99. Before December 7, the previous guide applies: check the version that matches your exam date on the official page. Anthropic offers a free prep course on the Academy.

domaines.nom: Define the task and write the prompt
domaines.fiche:
- A good prompt gives the **role**, the **context**, the **task**, the **expected format**, the constraints, and above all **what Claude doesn't know by default** (audience, stakes, sources).
- **Break down** a deliverable that is too big: successive prompts, follow-ups, a workflow in a Project, checkpoints between steps.
- **Diagnose** a disappointing answer: missing context, ambiguous instruction, missing constraint or wrong strategy. Then decide to iterate, start over or change approach.
- **AI Fluency** framework (the "4Ds"): **Delegation** (what to hand to AI), **Description** (describe well), **Discernment** (judge the results), **Diligence** (take responsibility).

questions.q: A project manager asks "Write me a summary of the meeting" and gets a generic text. What is the most likely cause?

options.t: Under-specification: audience, goal, format and source (the notes) weren't provided

questions.why: a generic answer usually comes from a prompt that doesn't say what Claude can't guess: context, goal, audience and format.

questions.q: In the AI Fluency framework, which skill is about deciding which work to hand to AI and which to keep for a human?
questions.why: Delegation is deciding which work should be done by humans, which by AI, and how to split the tasks.

questions.q: Which AI Fluency skill refers to critically evaluating AI outputs and behavior?
questions.why: Discernment means thoughtfully and critically evaluating AI outputs, processes and behaviors.

questions.q: An analyst must produce a 30-page market report with data, analysis and recommendations. Which approach is the most reliable?

options.t: Break it into steps (outline, research, analysis, writing by section) with a check between each step
Ask for everything in a single prompt and publish the result
Ask for the report three times and keep the longest

questions.why: a deliverable too big for a single request is broken into successive steps, with checkpoints between them.

questions.q: After three follow-ups, a conversation has gone in the wrong direction and Claude keeps repeating the same mistakes. What should you do?

options.t: Start a new conversation with a corrected prompt that includes what you learned
Keep following up forever in the same conversation

questions.why: when a conversation drifts, starting again with a better-specified prompt is often more effective than piling up corrections.

domaines.fiche:
- Judge an answer against its goal, its sources and professional standards: accurate, complete, relevant? Ready to use, to revise, or to be fixed by a human?
- **Hallucinations**: invented citations, precise numbers out of nowhere, inconsistencies, bias. You **check the source**, review citations, confirm **independently**. Asking Claude to confirm its own answer isn't independent verification.
- **Review level** by stakes: an internal draft and a customer document don't have the same requirements. Know when to escalate to a human.
- Adapt the format: an answer in the conversation, an artifact, structured data, a **calculation run by code** when the result must be exact, a document produced by a Skill.

questions.q: A Claude draft for a customer contains three percentages attributed to analyst firms and a quote from a competitor's executive. What should be done before sending it?

options.t: Check each number and the quote in the source documents or a reliable source, and remove or flag what can't be confirmed
Send it as is, since the sources are named
Ask Claude to add a "verified content" note

questions.why: precise numbers and attributed quotes are areas at risk of invention; independent verification is needed before an external deliverable, for which the author remains responsible.

questions.q: Why isn't asking Claude "Are you sure these numbers are accurate?" enough to validate them?

options.t: Because it isn't an independent confirmation: verification must go through the source or an external reference
Because Claude always refuses to answer
Because the question is too polite

questions.why: the model can confidently confirm invented information; only checking an independent source tells true from false.

questions.q: A Claude table must give exact totals over 5,000 rows of sales. Which approach guarantees reliable calculations?

options.t: Have the analysis run by code on the file, rather than a "mental" calculation in the answer
Ask Claude to estimate the totals
Paste the 5,000 rows into the prompt with no instruction

questions.why: Claude can run advanced analyses on uploaded data and produce spreadsheets with real formulas: the calculation is done by code, not estimated in the text.

questions.q: The same Claude answer serves as an internal draft for a team, then as the basis for a letter sent to a regulator. How should review be adapted?

options.t: Light review for the internal draft; full verification and human sign-off for the high-stakes external letter
The same quick review in both cases
Have only Claude review the letter

questions.why: the level of review depends on the consequence of an error and the document's destination; a high-stakes external deliverable needs full verification.

questions.q: A committee needs a shared, editable document produced from a conversation with Claude. Which output format fits?

options.t: An artifact (document, presentation…) that can be opened, edited and shared
A long answer in the conversation, copied by hand

questions.why: artifacts let you produce documents, presentations and designs you can edit and share, available on all plans.

questions.q: A Claude report cites a study published in 2024 that nobody can find. How do you describe this problem?

options.t: A possible hallucination (invented citation), to check before any use
A problem with memory being off
A limit on the number of connectors

questions.why: invented citations are among the ungrounded content to watch for; you confirm the source before using the information.

domaines.nom: Choose the capability, model and context
domaines.fiche:
- **Capabilities**: chat, **Projects** (persistent knowledge and instructions), **Artifacts**, **Research** (successive searches on the web and connected tools, with a sourced report), code-based analysis, **Skills** (procedures loaded as needed), **connectors**, **memory**.
- **Model and effort level**: a more capable model and more effort for a complex or high-stakes task; the faster, cheaper option when it's enough.
- **Context and memory**: know when to start over, summarize, save in a Project or rely on memory. Review, edit and delete memories; use **incognito chats** (not saved to history or memory, available **outside Projects**).

questions.q: A consultant wants an in-depth study: Claude must chain several searches, on the web and in her connected tools, and produce a report. Which capability should she choose?
questions.why: Research runs several searches that build on each other, on the web and connected tools, to study a question in depth.

questions.q: A user starts Research from the mobile app and is surprised her emails weren't consulted. Why?

options.t: On mobile, Research only searches the web and doesn't use connectors
A Project is needed to use Research

questions.why: the documentation states that Research started on mobile only searches the web, without using connectors or showing an error.

questions.q: To rephrase a sentence in an email, do you need the most capable model at maximum effort?

options.t: No: for a simple, low-risk task, the faster and cheaper option is the right choice
Yes, always the most capable model
Yes, otherwise the answer is wrong

questions.why: you match the model and effort to the complexity and stakes; a more capable model and high effort are for complex tasks.

questions.q: A consultant wants to discuss a personal topic without the conversation being saved to their history or to Claude's memory. What should they do?

options.t: Open an incognito chat, outside a Project
Open the conversation in a Project

questions.why: incognito chats are saved neither to history nor to memory; they are only available outside Projects.

questions.q: In a Project, a user wants one specific conversation not to use memory or add to it, while staying in the history. What should they do?

options.t: Turn off "Memory" in the "+" menu before sending the first message
Open an incognito chat in the Project

questions.why: incognito doesn't exist in Projects; you turn off memory for a conversation through the "+" menu before the first message, and the conversation stays in the history.

questions.q: In a Project, which memory does Claude use?

options.t: The Project's memory and the memory from conversations outside Projects, but not that of other Projects
The memory of all the user's Projects
The memory of other users in the organization

questions.why: each Project has its own memory; Claude uses it along with the memory outside Projects, but not that of other Projects.

domaines.fiche:
- End-to-end deliverables: the need, sourced research, data analysis by code, a synthesis into an action plan.
- **Delegation**: for each step of a process, decide "done by AI", "kept by a human" or "reviewed by a human", based on reversibility, stakes, the need for judgment or empathy, and accountability. Spot **over-delegation**.
- **Reusable workflows**: Projects, Skills, connectors, steps run by code; consistent results from one run and one user to the next; a workflow you can hand to a colleague.
- **Communicate** what Claude can and can't do reliably, without overstating or understating.

questions.q: In a hiring process, which step must stay under a human's responsibility?

options.t: The final hiring decision and announcing a rejection to the candidate
Summarizing the skills listed in a résumé
Preparing a list of interview questions

questions.why: high-stakes, irreversible decisions that require judgment and empathy stay human; preparation tasks can be handed to AI with review.

questions.q: A team produces the same report every week from the same sources, each person with their own prompts: results vary a lot. How do you make the workflow repeatable?

options.t: Create a Project with shared instructions and knowledge, and a Skill for the procedure, used by the whole team
Ask everyone to write longer prompts

questions.why: a Project brings shared knowledge and instructions; a Skill encodes the procedure, loaded when useful, for consistent results.

questions.q: A manager proposes letting Claude answer complaints from unhappy customers alone, without review, including granting refunds. What is the problem?

options.t: It's over-delegation: high-stakes, hard-to-reverse actions requiring judgment and empathy, with no human control
No problem, it's the best use of AI

questions.why: the delegation framework weighs reversibility, stakes, the need for empathy and accountability; here, human validation is required.

questions.q: An executive unfamiliar with AI asks whether Claude can "replace the legal team". Which answer is the most accurate?

options.t: Claude can speed up tasks (research, first drafts, summaries), but legal opinions are still validated by lawyers
No, Claude is useless for legal work

questions.why: you should present what Claude does reliably, the human oversight that remains and realistic outcomes, without overstating or understating.

questions.q: When is a Skill better suited than a custom instruction applied to every conversation?

options.t: For a task-specific procedure that should only load when it's useful

questions.why: custom instructions apply to every conversation; Skills are task-specific and only load when relevant.

domaines.fiche:
- **Project**: its own instructions, knowledge, Skills and memory. Context is **not shared between conversations** in a Project, except what's in the knowledge base. On paid plans, **RAG** expands knowledge capacity up to **10×**.
- Choosing between an **instruction** (constant behavior), **knowledge** (reference documents) and a **Skill** (procedure).
- **Connectors** (Google Drive, Gmail, Slack…): Claude **inherits each user's permissions**. Upload a file or connect a source; keep knowledge current and free of noise.
- **Degradation**: if quality drops, identify the layer at fault: instructions, document freshness, Skill version or accumulated memory.

questions.q: Two conversations take place in the same Project. Can the second rely on what was said in the first?

options.t: No, unless the information was added to the Project's knowledge base
Yes, always, all conversations are merged

questions.why: context isn't shared between a Project's conversations, except what is added to its knowledge base.

questions.q: A Project's knowledge is approaching the context limit. What happens on a paid plan?

options.t: Claude turns on RAG mode, which increases capacity up to 10 times while keeping quality
Nothing, you must create a second Project

questions.why: on paid plans, RAG kicks in when knowledge approaches the limit and expands capacity up to 10 times.

questions.q: A Google Drive connector is added. Can an employee get through Claude a file they don't have access to in Drive?

options.t: No: Claude inherits each person's permissions in the connected service
Yes, the connector sees the whole company Drive
Yes, if the Project is shared

questions.why: Claude inherits each user's permissions; if someone doesn't have access to a file, the connector can't reach it either.

questions.q: A Project's proposals have always been good, but lately they cite a pricing grid that was dropped. The instructions haven't changed. Which layer should you check first?

options.t: The freshness of the Project's knowledge: replace the outdated document
The instructions, to be rewritten entirely
The model, to be changed immediately

questions.why: an outdated document in the knowledge is the typical cause of stale information; identify the layer at fault before changing everything.

questions.q: A user has connected more than ten connectors and their conversations are running out of room. Which setting does the documentation suggest?
questions.why: with 10 or more active connectors, the documentation suggests "On demand" mode to leave more room for conversations.

domaines.nom: Responsible use, data protection and governance
domaines.fiche:
- **Use case fit**: suitable, suitable with safeguards, or unsuitable (with a justification), based on the task, delegation limits, trust in third-party Skills and connectors, and Anthropic's **Usage Policy**.
- **Data protection**: classify, **anonymize or pseudonymize before** uploading, think before sending a file for analysis, use memory controls and incognito according to the organization's policy. Incognito controls retention, **not** what is disclosed.
- **Policy and ethics**: spot departures from internal policy, bias, lack of transparency, tell a missing **rule** from a missing **training**, and choose the corrective action.

questions.q: Internal policy only allows AI analysis on de-identified data. An HR employee wants to analyze an export with names, addresses, salaries and free-text comments. What should she do?

options.t: De-identify the file before uploading it (remove names and addresses, code identifiers, check free-text comments)
Upload it as is in an incognito chat
Upload it to an HR-only Project
Ask Claude to anonymize it after the upload

questions.why: protection must happen before sharing; incognito limits retention but not disclosure, and anonymizing after upload means the data was already shared.

questions.q: A team wants to install a Skill found on an unknown third-party site, which asks for access to several connectors. What is the right approach?

options.t: Assess trust in this Skill (origin, content, requested rights) according to the organization's policy before installing it
Install it immediately, Skills are always safe
Share it with the whole organization to test it
Turn off memory and install it

questions.why: a Skill or plugin can greatly expand what Claude can do; judge its reliability before installing (the Enterprise plan can even scan Skills at install time).

questions.q: Several employees paste customer data into Claude although policy forbids it, because they don't know the rule. Which corrective action should you choose?

options.t: Train the teams on the existing policy: it's a lack of training, not a lack of rules

questions.why: you must tell a missing rule from missing training; here the rule exists but isn't known, so the fix is training.

examens.intro:
Anthropic's Claude architect certification, Foundations level: scoping and designing solutions with Claude (choice of model and platform, agentic architecture or single call, evaluation, cost, responsible deployment). Exam with Pearson VUE (online or at a test center), single- and multiple-choice questions, pass mark **720** on a 100 to 1000 scale. The exam is reserved for employees of Anthropic partners. The current guide is version 1.1 ("Effective November 2026"); this exam isn't one of the three Claude exams updated on December 7, 2026.

Anthropic recommends taking the free Academy courses first: they are summarized in the Claude course on this site (in French).

domaines.fiche:
**Workflows or agents** (Anthropic, *Building effective agents*)
- **Workflow**: a path defined by code (predictable). **Agent**: the model dynamically decides its steps and tools (flexible, more expensive, less predictable).
- Start simple: a well-designed single call is often enough; only add complexity if it improves the result.
- Patterns: **prompt chaining** (chained steps), **routing** (classify then direct), **parallelization** (sectioning or voting), **orchestrator-workers** (an orchestrator dynamically breaks down and delegates), **evaluator-optimizer** (one call generates, another evaluates and gives feedback).

**Subagents** (Claude Code): each has its **own context window**, system prompt, tools and permissions. Useful to isolate exploration and preserve the main context.

questions.q: A customer wants to classify each incoming ticket (billing, technical, sales) then handle it with a specialized prompt per category. Which pattern do you recommend?
questions.why: routing classifies the input and directs it to a specialized process; it fits when categories are distinct and better handled separately.

questions.q: A code change task touches a number of files that can't be predicted in advance. A central model must break down the task and delegate each part. Which pattern fits?
questions.why: in orchestrator-workers, a central LLM dynamically breaks down the task, delegates to workers and synthesizes the results; subtasks aren't defined in advance.

questions.q: A literary translation must be improved iteratively: one call translates, another critiques against clear criteria, then it starts again. Which pattern should you use?
questions.why: evaluator-optimizer has one call generate a response and another evaluate it, in a loop; it works well when clear evaluation criteria exist.

questions.q: What advice does Anthropic give before building a complex agentic system?

options.t: Look for the simplest possible solution and only add complexity when needed
Always start with a multi-agent system
Use as many tools as possible

questions.why: Anthropic recommends starting simple; agentic systems trade latency and cost for better performance, a trade-off that must be justified.

questions.q: For a security check, three independent calls analyze the same code and the majority result is kept. Which pattern is this?
questions.why: parallelization has two variants: sectioning (independent subtasks) and voting (the same task several times for varied outputs).

questions.q: Why hand a long code exploration to a subagent in Claude Code?

options.t: Because it works in its own context window and only returns the result, which preserves the main conversation's context
Because it has more permissions than the main agent by default

questions.why: each subagent runs in its own context window, with its own system prompt, tools and permissions.

questions.q: A monthly report always follows the same steps: extract, summarize, format. Workflow or agent?

options.t: A workflow (prompt chaining), because the steps are known and fixed
An autonomous agent, because it's more modern
Neither, a human must do everything

questions.why: prompt chaining fits when the task breaks down into fixed steps; it gains accuracy at the cost of a little latency.

questions.q: Where do you define a personal subagent, available in all of a developer's projects, with Claude Code?
questions.why: personal subagents go in ~/.claude/agents/; project subagents go in the repository's .claude/agents/.

domaines.fiche:
- **Tool use**: you describe each tool (name, clear **description**, **input_schema** in JSON Schema). Claude responds with a `tool_use` block and `stop_reason` = `tool_use`; **your code runs the tool** and returns a `tool_result`.
- Designing a good tool: a precise description of when to use it, explicit parameters, concise returns that are useful to the model.
- **MCP**: a standard protocol that connects an AI application to servers. Three server-side primitives: **tools** (actions), **resources** (data), **prompts** (reusable templates). Transports: **stdio** (local process) and **Streamable HTTP** (remote).
- In Claude Code: `claude mcp add`, local, project (shared `.mcp.json`) or user scope.

questions.q: Who runs the function when Claude decides to use a client tool defined in an API request?

options.t: The developer's application, which then returns the result in a tool_result block

questions.why: for client tools, Claude returns a tool_use block; the application runs the tool and returns the result in a tool_result message.

questions.q: Which `stop_reason` indicates that Claude is waiting for a tool's result?
questions.why: when Claude wants to use a tool, the response has a stop_reason of tool_use.

questions.q: What are the three primitives an MCP server can expose?
questions.why: an MCP server exposes tools (executable actions), resources (context data) and prompts (interaction templates).

questions.q: An MCP server must run locally, started by Claude Code as a subprocess. Which transport should you use?

options.t: Streamable HTTP behind a load balancer

questions.why: the stdio transport has client and server talk on the same machine through standard input and output; Streamable HTTP is for remote servers.

questions.q: Claude often picks the wrong tool between "search_orders" and "search_invoices". Which fix is the most effective?

options.t: Make the tool descriptions precise: what each does, when to use it, and its parameters

questions.why: the tool description is the main signal guiding Claude; detailed descriptions clearly improve tool choice.

questions.q: A team wants all its developers to have the same MCP server configured in Claude Code for a given repository. Which scope should it use?

options.t: Project scope, with a .mcp.json file versioned in the repository
Each developer's local scope, configured by hand

questions.why: project scope saves the configuration in .mcp.json at the project root, which you can version to share with the team.

domaines.fiche:
- **CLAUDE.md**: persistent instructions. Levels: organization (managed policy), **project** (`./CLAUDE.md`, shared through Git), **user** (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`). Imports with `@path/to/file`.
- **Permissions** (settings.json): `allow`, `ask`, `deny` rules; settings managed by the organization take precedence.
- **Hooks**: commands run at points in the lifecycle (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`…). Exit code **2** in `PreToolUse` **blocks** the tool call and sends the message back to Claude.
- **Skills** and commands, subagents, plugins to share a configuration.

questions.q: Where should you put personal preferences (commit style, shortcuts) that must apply to all of a developer's projects, without imposing them on the team?
questions.why: the user CLAUDE.md (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) holds personal preferences for all projects; the project one is shared by the team.

questions.q: How can a CLAUDE.md include the content of another file, for example the team's conventions?
questions.why: CLAUDE.md files can import other files with the @path/to/import syntax; their content is loaded into context.

questions.q: A PreToolUse hook must prevent any command that targets the production environment. How does the hook block the call?

options.t: By exiting with code 2, with the reason on standard error

questions.why: in a PreToolUse hook, exit code 2 blocks the tool call; the error message is sent back to Claude.

questions.q: When does a PostToolUse hook run?

options.t: Right after a tool has run successfully

questions.why: PostToolUse runs after a tool completes successfully, for example to run a formatter or tests.

questions.q: A team wants to forbid Claude Code from reading the project's .env files. What should it configure?

options.t: A deny rule in the settings.json permissions, for example on Read(./.env)
An allow rule on all files

questions.why: allow, ask and deny permission rules control tools and files; a deny rule prevents reading sensitive files.

questions.q: A company wants to enforce permission rules that developers can't override in their local settings. Which configuration level should it use?

options.t: Managed settings deployed by the organization

questions.why: managed settings have the highest precedence and can't be overridden by user or project settings.

domaines.fiche:
- Be **clear and direct**, give **context** and purpose, provide **examples** (few-shot), structure with **XML tags**, give a **role** through the system prompt, let Claude **think** before answering for complex tasks.
- **Structured outputs**: ask for a precise format; *structured outputs* constrain the response to a provided **JSON Schema**.
- Evaluate prompts with a test set and a score (eval) before changing them.

questions.q: An application must always receive from Claude JSON that matches a schema, with no missing field or surrounding text. Which feature should it use?

options.t: Structured outputs, with the expected JSON Schema
Ask "please answer in JSON" with no other control

questions.why: structured outputs constrain Claude's response to follow a provided JSON Schema.

questions.q: A prompt mixes instructions, a document to analyze and examples. Which technique helps Claude clearly tell these parts apart?

options.t: Wrap them in XML tags (for example <instructions>, <document>, <examples>)
Put the document after the question with no separation

questions.why: XML tags structure the prompt and avoid mixing up instructions, data and examples.

questions.q: Claude's answers don't have the desired tone or format despite a detailed description. Which technique is often the most effective?

options.t: Add a few examples of expected answers (few-shot / multishot)

questions.why: providing well-chosen examples shows Claude the expected format and style, which improves accuracy and consistency.

questions.q: Where do you define the expert role Claude should take for a whole conversation (for example "financial analyst")?
questions.why: the system prompt lets you give Claude a role, which improves accuracy and adapts the tone.

questions.q: Before rewriting a production prompt, how do you know whether the new version is really better?

options.t: Measure both versions on the same test set with defined success criteria (eval)
Test one question and trust your impression
Ask Claude which one it prefers

questions.why: Anthropic recommends defining success criteria and empirical evaluations before iterating on a prompt.

questions.q: For a complex multi-step analysis, which approach does Anthropic recommend with recent models?

options.t: Let Claude think before answering, with a general instruction such as "think thoroughly" or extended thinking, rather than a detailed hand-written plan
Forbid any thinking and demand an immediate answer

questions.why: the documentation states that an instruction like "think thoroughly" often gives better reasoning than a hand-written step-by-step plan, because Claude's reasoning often exceeds what a human would prescribe.

domaines.fiche:
- **Context window**: everything the model sees (system prompt, history, documents, tool results). It fills up: you must choose what goes in.
- **Prompt caching**: caches a reused prompt prefix (`cache_control`); lifetime of **5 minutes** by default, **1 hour** as an option at extra cost.
- **Message Batches**: asynchronous batch processing; results are available when everything is done or after **24 hours**, and the batch expires if it isn't finished within that time.
- Reliability: retries with backoff, output checks, continuous evaluation, human in the loop for risky actions.

questions.q: An application sends the same 50-page manual with every request, followed by a different question. How do you cut cost and latency?

options.t: Cache the manual with prompt caching (cache_control on the shared prefix)
Send the manual in several random pieces
Use a model with no context window

questions.why: prompt caching reuses an identical prefix from one request to the next, which reduces processing time and the cost of repeated parts.

questions.q: What is the default lifetime of a prompt cache entry?

options.t: 5 minutes, with a 1-hour option at extra cost

questions.why: the cache has a default lifetime of 5 minutes; a 1-hour duration is available at extra cost.

questions.q: A company must classify 100,000 customer reviews by tomorrow, with no need for an immediate response. Which approach fits?

options.t: The Message Batches API, with results available within 24 hours at most
100,000 parallel synchronous calls with no control
A single prompt containing all the reviews

questions.why: the Message Batches API processes requests in batches asynchronously; results are available when everything is done or after 24 hours.

questions.q: In a long agent session, the context window fills with bulky tool results. Which architecture good practice should you apply?

options.t: Keep only what's useful in context: concise tool results, summaries, or delegation to subagents that return a summary
Add even more documents to be safe

questions.why: the context window is limited; everything that goes in (including tool results) uses space, so it must be actively managed.

examens.intro:
The Claude certification for developers: integrating the Messages API and SDKs, building agents and workflows (Claude Agent SDK), using and extending Claude Code, designing prompts and context, tools and MCP servers, evaluating and debugging, choosing models and optimizing cost, and applying security by design.

Outline from **guide version 1.1, effective December 7, 2026**: 70 questions (60 scored, 10 unscored), 120 minutes, multiple-choice scenarios, pass mark **720** on 100–1000, USD 125. Before December 7, the previous guide applies: check the version that matches your exam date. The *Building with the Claude API* course in this site's Claude section (in French) covers a large part of the outline.

domaines.fiche:
- **Workflow or agent**: a workflow (path defined by code, predictable, auditable) when the task is well defined; an agent (the model chooses its steps) when you need flexibility and model-driven decisions.
- Orchestrator / subagent split; execution environment: a self-hosted harness or a managed, isolated agent runtime (Claude Managed Agents).
- **Agent SDK and hooks**: mandatory actions (checks, logging, blocks) go through **hooks**, run **deterministically**, not left to the model's judgment. A `PreToolUse` hook can return `permissionDecision: "deny"`.
- Diagnosing a failing agent: a tool loop that never stops, poorly isolated subagents, memory, context window management.

questions.q: A bank complaint process must follow fixed steps, be auditable and always take the same path for the same input. Which architecture do you recommend?

options.t: A workflow, with steps defined by code
An autonomous agent that freely chooses its tools
A single prompt with no structure

questions.why: workflows offer predictability and consistency for well-defined tasks; agents fit when flexibility and model-driven decisions are needed.

questions.q: An agent built with the Claude Agent SDK must refuse any change to .env files, whatever instructions it receives. How do you guarantee this?

options.t: With a PreToolUse hook that returns permissionDecision "deny" for these operations
By adding "never touch .env files" to the system prompt
By asking the agent to review itself

questions.why: a hook runs deterministically before the tool call and can block the operation; an instruction in the prompt can be ignored or bypassed.

questions.q: An agent keeps calling the same search tool and never manages to answer. Which design element should you review first?

options.t: The tool loop's stopping condition (iteration limit, end criterion, usable tool results)
The model name in the logs

questions.why: agents run in a loop with tool feedback; you need stopping conditions (for example a maximum number of iterations) to keep control.

questions.q: A main agent delegates the analysis of large log files. How do you keep these logs from filling its context?

options.t: Hand the analysis to a subagent that works in its own context window and only returns a summary
Copy all the logs into the system prompt

questions.why: a subagent has its own context window; only its result comes back into the main context.

questions.q: In the Claude Agent SDK, at which moments can hooks step in?

options.t: At lifecycle events: before a tool call (PreToolUse), after its result (PostToolUse), when a subagent starts or stops…
Only at the end of the session

questions.why: the SDK fires events (tool about to be called, tool finished, subagent started or stopped…) that hooks can respond to.

domaines.fiche:
- **Messages API**: message structure, tools, **streaming**, vision, thinking, **prompt caching**, structured output, **stop_reason**. Choosing between real time and **Message Batches**.
- **Streaming**: `message_start`, then for each block `content_block_start` / `content_block_delta` / `content_block_stop`, then `message_delta` (which carries the `stop_reason`) and **`message_stop`**, the final event.
- **Errors**: **429** `rate_limit_error`, **529** `overloaded_error` (retry with backoff), **400** `invalid_request_error` (fix the request, don't retry it as is).
- Configuration and SDLC: CLAUDE.md, settings.json, pinning the model version, prompt versioning, CI integration; **Files API** for documents.

questions.q: A streaming application considers the response finished at the first content_block_stop. Responses containing text and then a tool call get truncated. Which event really marks the end of the message?
questions.why: content_block_stop closes a single block; a message can contain several. message_stop is the message's final event.

questions.q: In streaming, where does the application read the stop reason (for example max_tokens or end_turn)?
questions.why: the message_delta event carries the final stop_reason; message_start shows it as null.

questions.q: An integration gets a 529 overloaded_error. Which reaction is correct?

options.t: Retry later with exponential backoff, since the overload is temporary
Fix the request format, since it's invalid
Treat the response as permanently impossible

questions.why: 529 signals that the API is temporarily overloaded; unlike a 400 error, the same request may succeed later.

questions.q: A request returns 400 invalid_request_error. The retry logic resends it ten times unchanged. What is the flaw?

options.t: A 400 error comes from the request's format or content: it must be fixed, not resent as is
The API key should be changed

questions.why: 400 signals a problem with the request's format or content; retries must tell this error apart from temporary errors (429, 529).

questions.q: A service must classify 200,000 documents overnight, with no need for an immediate response. Which API option should it choose?

options.t: The Message Batches API, with results available within 24 hours at most
A single message containing all the documents

questions.why: batches process requests asynchronously; results are available when everything is done or after 24 hours.

questions.q: An application gets a 429 rate_limit_error during a traffic spike. What does it mean?

options.t: The organization hit a rate limit (or a spend limit): slow down and retry later

questions.why: 429 indicates that a rate limit or the usage tier's spend limit has been reached.

domaines.fiche:
- Works on CLI, desktop, IDE, web and mobile; hierarchy and precedence of **CLAUDE.md** files (organization, project, user); **settings.json**; permission modes; headless and streaming modes.
- Extensions: **Skill**, **plugin**, rules file, **hook**, **subagent**, command: choose the right mechanism for a team workflow, write it and distribute it.

questions.q: A team wants every file change by Claude Code to be followed by formatting, guaranteed. Which mechanism should it choose?

options.t: A PostToolUse hook that runs the formatter
A sentence in CLAUDE.md asking to format
A formatting subagent called when Claude thinks it useful

questions.why: a hook runs automatically on every targeted event; an instruction in CLAUDE.md is left to the model's judgment.

questions.q: A team wants to distribute a consistent set to all its developers: skills, hooks, subagents and MCP servers. Which Claude Code mechanism is designed for this?
questions.why: plugins bundle skills, connectors, hooks and subagents into a single package that you distribute.

domaines.fiche:
- Design an **evaluation** tied to a quality goal: a **golden set**, regression tests, behavior checks, an **LLM-as-judge** calibrated on human labels, defensible metrics.
- **Diagnose** a failure from a trace: hallucination, refusal, under-action, context loss, format drift, inconsistency. Tell whether it comes from the integration or the model, and fix the cause.

questions.q: A team wants to automatically score the quality of free-form answers (tone, completeness) on 500 cases. Which method should it use, and how does it make it reliable?

options.t: An LLM-as-judge with a clear rubric, calibrated by comparing its scores to a sample scored by humans
Asking the evaluated model to score itself, unchecked

questions.why: LLM grading fits subjective criteria; you must check that it agrees with human judgment before relying on it.

questions.q: A ticket classifier must return one category out of six. Which evaluation method is the simplest and most reliable?

options.t: An exact match with the expected answer from a golden set

questions.why: when the expected answer is a precise value, an exact match with a reference answer is fast and reliable.

questions.q: An integration's JSON outputs fail parsing about once in fifty, although the model's answer is right in substance. Where does the fix belong?

options.t: On the format and integration side: structured outputs with a strict schema, validation and defensive parsing

questions.why: format drift is fixed by constraining output to a JSON Schema and validating the response before using it.

domaines.fiche:
- Tokens, context window, sampling and non-determinism; **adaptive thinking** and **effort level**: the `effort` parameter trades answer thoroughness against token economy.
- Choose the **model tier** for quality, latency and cost; prepare version changes with **regression evaluations**.
- Cutting costs: **prompt caching** (cache of an identical **prefix**, up to **4 cache breakpoints**, 5-minute or 1-hour lifetime), **batches**, token budgets.

questions.q: Every request sends the same long system prompt and the same tool definitions, then a different question. Input costs dominate. What should you do?

options.t: Put a cache breakpoint after the shared prefix (system prompt and tools) with cache_control
Put the cache breakpoint after the user's question

questions.why: the cache reuses an identical prefix; a breakpoint placed after the variable part makes each prefix unique and prevents any reuse.

questions.q: How many cache breakpoints can you define in a request?
questions.why: you can define up to 4 cache breakpoints, for example to separate parts that change at different rates.

questions.q: A simple classification task uses far too many thinking tokens. Which setting reduces spend without changing models?
questions.why: the effort parameter controls how many tokens Claude spends, trading thoroughness against economy.

questions.q: Before moving to a new model version in production, how do you limit the risk of behavior changes?

options.t: Rerun the regression evaluations on the new version and compare, while pinning the current version until then

questions.why: you define success criteria and empirical tests, which you rerun to compare versions before switching.

domaines.fiche:
- **Long sessions**: context that bloats or drifts. Remedies: **compaction** (server-side summary to stay within the window), pruning tool results, isolation in subagents, a new session.
- **Revising a prompt** from evaluations: clarity, system or user placement, examples (zero, one or several), output constraints, input cleanup.
- **Structured output** with a strict schema, validation and defensive parsing.
- **Grounding and citations**: answer from the provided documents, cite the source, answer "not found" if the information isn't there. Full context or passage retrieval depending on the corpus's size, cost and freshness.

questions.q: An agent working for several hours ends up exceeding its context window. Which API feature lets it stay within the window without writing its own summarization code?
questions.why: compaction summarizes context on the server side, which keeps a long conversation or agent task within the context window with no summarization code.

questions.q: An assistant must answer only from the provided contracts and say precisely where each answer comes from. Which API feature should it use?

options.t: Citations, which return the exact passages from the documents

questions.why: with citations, Claude references the passages of the provided documents; the cited text (cited_text) doesn't count toward output tokens.

questions.q: What should a document-grounded assistant do when the answer isn't in the documents?

options.t: Say so clearly ("not found in the documents") instead of making up an answer
Search the internet without saying so

questions.why: the outline calls for queries that ground answers in the documents, cite the source and return "not found" when the information is missing.

questions.q: A format instruction is often ignored because it's buried in the middle of a long user message full of data. Which revision is the most effective?

options.t: Separate data from instructions (XML tags) and put lasting rules in the system prompt
Repeat the instruction in capitals ten times

questions.why: structuring the prompt with XML tags and placing instructions well avoids mixing up instructions and data.

questions.q: A model must produce a very particular response format that is hard to describe. Which revision technique helps most?

options.t: Add a few examples of the expected format (few-shot)
Cut the prompt to one word

questions.why: well-chosen examples show the expected format and style and improve consistency.

domaines.fiche:
- **Prompt injection** and jailbreak: an agent that reads untrusted content (web pages, emails, documents) needs **layered** protections to avoid data leaks and unwanted actions.
- **Deterministic guardrails** and **least privilege**: hooks block destructive actions even under adversarial instructions.
- **API keys**: never in client code; calls through a **server-side proxy**, workspace keys rather than admin keys, separate environments, **environment variables** or a secrets manager, **regular rotation**, access monitoring.

questions.q: A mobile app calls the Claude API directly with the key embedded in the app. What is the right fix?

options.t: Go through a server (proxy) that holds the key and calls the API; the key is never shipped to the client
Encrypt the key in the app's code

questions.why: a key shipped in a client can be extracted; best practices recommend keeping keys server-side, in environment variables or a secrets manager.

questions.q: Which practice does Anthropic recommend to limit the impact of a compromised API key?

options.t: Rotate keys regularly and monitor their usage
Use the same key for all environments
Publish the key in the repository to find it easily

questions.why: regular key rotation (for example every 90 days) and monitoring shrink the exposure window.

domaines.fiche:
- **Designing a tool**: function schema, a **very detailed description** (by far the most important factor), a minimal, usable result, error handling, where it runs, approval model.
- **MCP server**: resources, tools and prompts; **stdio** or **HTTP** transport; authentication.
- **Choosing the mechanism**: built-in tool, custom tool, **Skill** or **MCP server**, based on where the capability should live, who maintains it and how Claude discovers it.
- `tool_choice`: `auto`, `any` (at least one tool), `tool` (a specific tool), `none`.

questions.q: According to Anthropic's documentation, what is the most important factor for Claude to use a tool well?

options.t: An extremely detailed description: what the tool does, when to use it, what each parameter means
A large number of optional parameters

questions.why: the documentation states that very detailed descriptions are by far the most important factor in tool performance.

questions.q: An application must force Claude to call at least one of the provided tools, without imposing which. Which tool_choice value should it use?
questions.why: "any" forces the use of one of the provided tools; "tool" imposes a specific tool; "auto" lets the model decide.

questions.q: A team wants to make the same internal data source available to Claude Code, Claude Desktop and several agents, maintained in one place by the data team. Which mechanism should it choose?

options.t: An MCP server, which each client connects to
A Skill copied into each project
A custom tool recoded in each application

questions.why: MCP connects an AI application to servers that expose tools and resources; one server, maintained in one place, serves several clients.

examens.intro:
The advanced Claude architect certification: designing, integrating and governing Claude solutions in production. You reason from artifacts (architectures, logs, traces, evaluation results) to choose the deployment surface, the agent runtime, the integration, the security and compliance controls, and to communicate decisions.

Outline from **guide version 1.1, effective December 7, 2026**: 70 questions (60 scored, 10 unscored), 120 minutes, multiple-choice scenarios, pass mark **720** on 100–1000, USD 175. The CCAR-F scope is assumed. Before December 7, the previous guide applies.

domaines.fiche:
- **Delegation** to Claude, a human or collaboration, based on reversibility, stakes and accountability.
- Assess an end-to-end architecture (input, processing, output, feedback loop): scalability, maintainability, access control, the first component to give way under load.
- Choose the pattern: **workflow**, **agent**, **augmented LLM**, **Skills**. Orchestrator / subagent split with observability and error recovery.
- **Deployment surface**: Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry. **Agent runtime**: Messages API loop, self-hosted Agent SDK or headless Claude Code, Claude Managed Agents. Trade off data residency, compliance, model and feature availability, and who owns operations and session state.

questions.q: A bank must keep all model inputs within the perimeter of its cloud provider, where it holds its residency attestations. Which option meets this constraint, and what trade-off does it imply?

options.t: Use its cloud provider's Claude surface; accept that some features arrive later and that it owns running the runtime
Use the Anthropic API with zero retention, which solves residency
Duplicate the documents in both clouds

questions.why: residency requires the cloud provider's surface; on these surfaces, model availability varies by region and new features don't always arrive the same day as on Anthropic's platform. Zero retention governs how long data is kept, not where it is processed.

questions.q: Why isn't a zero data retention (ZDR) setup enough to meet a data residency obligation?

options.t: Because ZDR is about retaining prompts and responses, not where they are processed
Because ZDR encrypts data with a public key
Because ZDR only exists on mobile

questions.why: with ZDR, prompts and responses aren't stored; that says nothing about where processing happens, which depends on the deployment surface.

questions.q: A contract termination process includes: reading the request, looking up the account, calculating penalties, sending the termination notice to the customer. Which step must stay validated by a human?

options.t: Sending the termination notice, a high-stakes, hard-to-reverse action
None, the agent can do everything alone

questions.why: delegation is decided by reversibility, stakes and accountability; reads with no side effects can be automated.

questions.q: A team is torn between an autonomous agent and a workflow to handle highly standardized requests audited by a regulator. What do you recommend?

options.t: A workflow: a path defined by code, predictable and auditable
A multi-agent system from the start
A free conversation with a model

questions.why: workflows offer predictability and consistency for well-defined tasks; agents are justified when flexibility is needed.

questions.q: An agent platform must keep session history and be able to resume an interrupted run, with a self-hosted runtime. Which Agent SDK feature should it use?

options.t: Session persistence, with resume or fork of a previous run
A new model on every resume

questions.why: the Agent SDK keeps conversation history and lets you continue, resume or fork a previous run.

domaines.fiche:
- Choose the model tier that meets **all** latency, cost and quality constraints.
- Diagnose an under-specified system prompt; choose the technique (zero or few examples, guided reasoning or native thinking, structured output).
- Token economics: context composition, **caching** (stable content before variable content, up to 4 cache breakpoints), packaging into Skills.
- Long sessions: reasoning effort, **context editing** (automatic clearing of the oldest tool results), **memory tool** (files under `/memories`, read back from one conversation to the next), **compaction**.

questions.q: An agent makes hundreds of tool calls. Old, now useless results saturate the context. Which API feature addresses exactly this case?

options.t: Context editing, which automatically clears the oldest tool results

questions.why: tool result clearing suits tool-heavy agentic workflows; the API clears the oldest results in chronological order.

questions.q: An agent must recall what it learned about a project from one conversation to the next, over several weeks. Which feature should it use?

options.t: The memory tool, which stores files under /memories and reads them back in later conversations
A longer system prompt on every call

questions.why: with the memory tool, Claude saves what it learns in files under /memories and reads them later to continue the work.

questions.q: A repeated sequence has a stable system prompt, a customer document that changes a few times a day, then the question. How should you place the cache breakpoints?

options.t: One breakpoint after the stable part and a second after the customer document, so each prefix is reused at its own rate
A single breakpoint after the question
No breakpoint: caching is automatic for everything
A breakpoint before the system prompt

questions.why: the cache reuses an identical prefix; put stable content before variable content, and you can define up to 4 cache breakpoints.

questions.q: For a complex, high-value task, the team is torn between a very detailed hand-written reasoning plan and a general thinking instruction. What does the documentation recommend for recent models?

options.t: A general instruction ("think thoroughly") or native thinking often gives better reasoning than a prescribed plan

questions.why: the documentation states that an instruction like "think thoroughly" often produces better reasoning than a hand-written step-by-step plan.

domaines.fiche:
- **Least privilege**: remove, restrict or replace unneeded tool connections; risks of credential exposure and privilege escalation.
- Lift the **dominant constraint** (accuracy or latency) at the least cost to the other.
- Close the **instrumentation gaps** that let a failure through.
- **Retrieval**: a RAG pipeline, agentic search with tools, or the full corpus in context. **Contextual Retrieval**: context added to chunks before embeddings and BM25.
- **Connection mechanism**: MCP, direct API or CLI, handoff between agents.
- **Progressive discovery** (load tools on demand, *tool search*) or loading everything into context.
- **Reliability**: rate limit handling, retry with backoff, **idempotency** of tools with side effects, fallback routing.

questions.q: An agent pays expense reports through a tool. After a spike of errors, requests that timed out on the client side are replayed although the payment had already gone through: some employees are paid twice. Which fix is the most direct?

options.t: Make the payment tool idempotent (idempotency key) so a replayed request doesn't repeat the action
Increase the timeout and reduce the number of retries
Add an instruction to the prompt: "check before paying"

questions.why: a retry is only safe if the operation is idempotent; otherwise it may run several times.

questions.q: An agent has 400 tools, and their definitions fill a large part of the context on every request. Which approach do you recommend?

options.t: Progressive discovery with the tool search tool (defer_loading), which only loads the tools needed
Load all 400 definitions on every call

questions.why: the tool search tool lets you handle hundreds or thousands of tools; tools marked defer_loading are only loaded when they're found.

questions.q: A document assistant often misses passages that contain exact product codes. Which retrieval improvement has Anthropic documented?

options.t: Contextual Retrieval: add context to chunks before embeddings and BM25, optionally with reranking
Cut the number of documents to one

questions.why: Contextual Embeddings and Contextual BM25 clearly reduce retrieval failures, even more so with reranking.

questions.q: A support agent has read and write access to the whole CRM, while it should only consult the account of the current ticket. What is the architect's recommendation?

options.t: Apply least privilege: restrict access to the ticket's account and remove unneeded write access
Keep all rights for more flexibility
Add a caution instruction to the prompt
Grant administrator rights to avoid errors

questions.why: agents' access to tools and data must be limited to what is strictly necessary; an instruction in the prompt isn't a barrier.

questions.q: An integration gets 429s during peaks. How does the documentation measure the rate limits to monitor?

options.t: In requests per minute (RPM), input tokens per minute (ITPM) and output tokens per minute (OTPM), per model class

questions.why: limits are measured in RPM, ITPM and OTPM for each model class; you must identify which one is the dominant constraint.

questions.q: A stable 50-page corpus is queried a few times a day. Do you need a full RAG pipeline?

options.t: Not necessarily: a small, stable corpus can be provided entirely in context (with caching), simpler than an index
No, you must fine-tune a model
You need one vector database per page

questions.why: Anthropic states that below about 200,000 tokens (about 500 pages), you can include the whole knowledge base in the prompt, with no RAG, using prompt caching to limit cost.

domaines.fiche:
- After a production failure: which metric dimension was missing (accuracy, grounding, latency, cost, safety)?
- Derive evaluations from the **business process** and the success criterion.
- **LLM-as-judge**: a clear rubric, calibration on human labels.
- Comparing two configurations: several trials per case to separate the effect from run-to-run variance.
- Find the root cause in traces: prompt, retrieval, hallucination, tool, subagent or model.
- Optimize cost and latency (cache hit rate). **Model migration**: pin, retune prompts, rebuild the evaluation baseline or defer, according to the deprecation schedule.

questions.q: An answer not grounded in the documents reached production although all evaluations were green. The tests only measured relevance. Which dimension was missing?

options.t: Groundedness: the answer's faithfulness to the provided sources

questions.why: an answer can be relevant without being grounded in the sources; you need a groundedness metric to catch this kind of failure before production.

questions.q: Claude's outputs aren't deterministic. How do you compare two prompt versions in an interpretable way?

options.t: Run several trials per test case to separate the version's effect from run-to-run variance
Compare on a single hand-picked question
Ask the model which version it prefers

questions.why: with variable outputs, you need enough trials per case and defined success criteria to draw conclusions.

questions.q: A model used in production has an announced retirement date. Which approach do you recommend?

options.t: Check the deprecations page, pin the current version, rerun regression evaluations on the replacement version, retune prompts before the retirement date
Wait for the retirement and see what happens

questions.why: the deprecations page gives retirement dates and recommended replacements; the migration is driven by regression evaluations within that window.

questions.q: An LLM judge used as a release gate approves every new version, while users see no improvement. What should you do first?

options.t: Measure the judge's agreement with human labels and remove its gate authority while agreement is insufficient
Add more cases without checking the judge

questions.why: an LLM-based grader must be validated against human judgment before you rely on its verdicts.

questions.q: An assistant's traces show that the right documents are never retrieved, while the model answers correctly when given the right passages. Where is the root cause?

options.t: In retrieval (indexing, chunking, query), not in the model
In the model, which must be changed

questions.why: if the model answers correctly with the right passages, the failure comes from the retrieval step; that's what must be fixed.

domaines.fiche:
- Place **guardrails** where they close the abuse path without hindering legitimate use.
- **Prompt injection**: retrieved documents, tool results, MCP server responses, third-party Skills. Untrusted content must never be treated as an instruction. Input filters (*harmlessness screens*), hardened system prompts, safe handling of tool content.
- Classify risks: attack surface, failures, token and quota exhaustion, supply chain.
- **Human in the loop** on irreversible or high-stakes actions, without blocking acceptable-risk paths.
- Compliance: residency and surface, **retention and ZDR**, PII detection and masking, audit logs, tenant isolation.
- Bias: tell data bias, prompt wording bias and evaluation design bias apart.

questions.q: An account change agent chains six steps, including a subscription change that triggers an immediate charge. A human approval before every tool call creates hours of waiting. What do you recommend?

options.t: Keep an approval before the subscription change only (irreversible), and let reads and reversible actions run with logging
Keep the approval before every step
Let the agent ask for approval only when it feels unsure

questions.why: where approvals go depends on reversibility and stakes; an irreversible action requires a deterministic gate, not the model's self-assessment.

questions.q: An agent's architecture injects web pages, MCP server responses and third-party Skills into its context. Which control principle should you apply?

options.t: Treat all this content as untrusted: it must never be interpreted as an instruction, with input filtering and safe handling of tool content
Add a single caution sentence to the prompt

questions.why: the documentation recommends input filtering, hardened system prompts and safe handling of untrusted tool content.

questions.q: How do you cheaply filter malicious user inputs before they reach the main agent?

options.t: An input screen (harmlessness screen) with a lightweight model that pre-analyzes the request
The most capable model for every filter
No filter, the main model is enough
A manual human filter on every message

questions.why: the documentation suggests using a lightweight model to pre-screen inputs before the main conversation.

questions.q: A healthcare customer requires that prompts and responses not be retained by the provider. Which architectural control should you document?

options.t: A zero data retention (ZDR) setup on the features that support it

questions.why: with ZDR, prompts and outputs aren't stored; the documentation specifies, feature by feature, what is retained.

questions.q: The most cited reference framework for classifying the risks of LLM-based applications is:

options.t: The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (including LLM01: Prompt Injection)

questions.why: the OWASP Gen AI Security Project publishes a Top 10 of LLM application risks, including prompt injection (LLM01).

domaines.fiche:
- Spot an **untenable commitment** in a requirements document or an SLA (for example "100% accuracy"), and propose the clarification or architecture change.
- Write **ADRs** (Architecture Decision Records) that make the trade-off and the residual risk explicit, without overstating certainty about model behavior.
- A complete **handover** package: assumptions, dependencies, runbook.

questions.q: A draft SLA promises "100% accurate answers" for a generative assistant. What is the architect's reaction?

options.t: Flag that this is untenable for a generative system, and propose a measurable goal (a rate measured on an evaluation set) with human review on risky cases
Remove any quality measure from the contract

questions.why: a model's outputs aren't guaranteed; commitments must rest on success criteria measured by evaluations.

questions.q: An operations team takes over a Claude system in production. Which missing item will block operations fastest?

options.t: The runbook: procedures for 429/529 errors, a retired model, quality drift, with dependencies and contacts

questions.why: a handover must cover assumptions, dependencies and the runbook; without procedures for documented errors and model retirements, the team can't run the system.

domaines.fiche:
- Distribute a proven Claude Code workflow: **plugin** (skills, hooks, subagents, commands, MCP configuration), **marketplace**, **managed settings**; decide what is enforced centrally.
- Configure Claude Code or the Agent SDK: **permission modes** (default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions), hooks, subagents, headless or CI mode.
- Keep **human accountability** for AI-generated code (review, ownership).

questions.q: A CI pipeline must run Claude Code unattended, allowing only tools approved in advance. Which permission mode fits?

options.t: dontAsk, which only allows pre-approved tools
acceptEdits, which approves all file changes

questions.why: dontAsk only allows pre-approved tools without prompting; bypassPermissions skips all checks, which is risky when unattended.

questions.q: The organization wants to impose on all teams certain Claude Code rules (permissions, allowed MCP servers) that can't be overridden locally. Where should they be defined?

options.t: In managed settings (managed-settings.json) deployed by the organization

questions.why: managed settings have the highest precedence in Claude Code's configuration hierarchy.

questions.q: A team adopts AI-assisted development. Which control preserves human accountability for generated code?

options.t: A mandatory human review before merging, with a named owner for each change
Automatically merge any code that compiles
Let the AI approve its own changes

questions.why: the Claude Code documentation reminds that the user remains responsible for reviewing proposed code and commands before approving them; a mandatory human review and a named owner formalize that accountability.

examens.intro:
The Claude certification for people who **run** Claude systems in production: observability, diagnosis and incident management, continuous evaluation, cost and latency at scale, guardrails and security, durable agent orchestration, and running fleets of coding agents.

Outline from **guide version 1.0** ("Effective November 2026", no update announced for December 7): 70 questions (60 scored, 10 unscored), 120 minutes, single and multiple choice, pass mark **720** on 100–1000, USD 175. The CCDV-F scope is assumed. November 1, used as the outline date, is a convention: the guide only says "November 2026".

domaines.fiche:
- Multi-agent orchestration: supervisor and workers, parallel subagents, delegation and context isolation boundaries, human approvals.
- **Durable execution**: session persistence, checkpoints, resuming after an interruption or a model version change.
- Evolving a system between workflow and agent based on production data.
- **Context policy**: compaction, context editing, persistent memory, a tool catalog kept out of context (tool search).

questions.q: A data migration agent runs for several hours and must be able to resume after a server restart without starting over. Which Agent SDK capability should it use?

options.t: Session persistence, with resume of a previous run

questions.why: the Agent SDK keeps conversation history and lets you continue, resume or fork a previous run.

questions.q: An agent regularly approaches its context window limit during long tasks. Which API option keeps the conversation within the window without home-made summarization code?
questions.why: compaction runs on the server side and keeps a long conversation or agent task within the context window, with no summarization code to write.

questions.q: An agent has a catalog of 800 internal tools. How do you keep their definitions from taking up context on every request?

options.t: Mark the tools as defer_loading and use the tool search tool
Load all definitions on every call

questions.why: the tool search tool lets you scale to hundreds or thousands of tools; defer_loading tools are only loaded when they're found.

questions.q: A multi-step agent accumulates bulky tool results that are no longer useful. Which feature removes them automatically, from oldest to newest?
questions.why: once enabled, context editing automatically clears the oldest tool results and replaces them with placeholder text.

questions.q: A team must choose between keeping a fixed workflow or moving to an agent for a production process. What should the decision rest on?

options.t: Production data (cost, reliability, quality): the agent is only justified if flexibility brings a measurable gain

questions.why: agentic systems trade latency and cost for better performance; this trade-off must be justified by results.

domaines.fiche:
- **Resilience**: retry with backoff, circuit breakers, graceful degradation, fallbacks between models, regions or platforms. Tell apart a **rate limit**, a **refusal** (`stop_reason` = `refusal`) and **context overflow** (`model_context_window_exceeded`).
- **Throughput**: RPM, ITPM, OTPM limits; queueing and backpressure; batches; per-tenant quotas.
- **MCP in production and change management**: remote deployment and authentication, tool versioning, model migrations, prompt versioning, progressive rollout with rollback.
- **Grounding at scale**: agentic search or RAG, chunking, hybrid search, reranking, citations and stating uncertainty.

questions.q: A fallback policy retries every failed request on a second model. The traces mix rate limits, responses cut at max_tokens and refusals. Which fix improves reliability?

options.t: Handle each cause separately: backoff for rate limits, a higher output budget for max_tokens, specific handling (documented fallback) for refusals
Increase the number of retries for everything
Route all traffic to the fallback model

questions.why: these stop conditions are different: max_tokens requires raising the limit or continuing, refusal is handled through stop_details and a fallback model, and a rate limit is handled with backoff.

questions.q: A response arrives with the stop_reason model_context_window_exceeded. How should you handle it?

options.t: As truncated: the response filled the model's context window

questions.why: this stop_reason means the response filled the context window; the documentation says to treat it as truncated.

questions.q: A multi-tenant platform must prevent one heavy customer from exhausting everyone else's rate limits. Which approach do you recommend?

options.t: Per-tenant quotas, a queue with backpressure, and tracking of the RPM, ITPM and OTPM limits
Let each customer call without limit
A single shared account with no tracking

questions.why: limits are measured in requests and tokens per minute; per-tenant isolation and backpressure protect the other customers.

questions.q: A new system prompt must be deployed to production on a critical service. Which approach limits the risk?

options.t: Version the prompt, validate it with evaluations, roll it out progressively to part of the traffic with a rollback ready
Replace it directly for all users
Edit it in production with no record

questions.why: prompt and model changes are managed like releases: versioning, regression tests, progressive rollout, rollback.

questions.q: A knowledge base assistant fails to find passages containing exact references. Which combination improves retrieval according to Anthropic?

options.t: Contextual embeddings and BM25 (Contextual Retrieval), with reranking

questions.why: Contextual Retrieval combines contextual embeddings and BM25; with reranking, retrieval failures drop even further.

questions.q: A document-grounded answer can't find the requested information. Which behavior should you design?

options.t: State the uncertainty or "not found", and cite the sources used when an answer is given

questions.why: grounding means citing source passages and flagging missing information rather than inventing it.

domaines.fiche:
- **Telemetry**: distributed traces of agent loops and tool calls, token and cost metrics, cache diagnostics, structured logs; content capture compatible with ZDR.
- **SLIs and SLOs**, alerts, dashboards; detecting quality drift, especially after a model update.
- Trace analysis at scale: sampling, aggregation, failure cohort analysis.
- Claude Code exposes metrics and events through **OpenTelemetry** (session, cost, token counters…).

questions.q: The organization wants to track the cost and tokens used by Claude Code in all its existing observability tools. Which feature should it use?

options.t: Claude Code's OpenTelemetry export (cost and token counters, and events)

questions.why: Claude Code can export metrics (cost, token, session counters…) and events through OpenTelemetry.

questions.q: After a model update, quality drops for one category of requests, with no technical error. Which setup would have caught it?

options.t: Production quality monitoring (evaluated traffic sampling, quality SLIs) with an alert on drift

questions.why: quality drift produces no technical error; you must measure quality itself, with defined criteria, on real traffic.

questions.q: A customer under zero data retention (ZDR) wants detailed traces for debugging. Which precaution should you take?

options.t: Configure trace content capture consistently with the retention requirements (for example, don't log the text of prompts and responses)
Store prompts in a public file

questions.why: with ZDR, prompts and responses aren't stored on the provider's side; the application's instrumentation must respect the same requirement.

questions.q: Users find the assistant slow although total response time is stable. Which metric should you track first?

options.t: Time to first token (TTFT), which drives perceived responsiveness

questions.why: TTFT measures the time until the first token is generated; it's what streaming improves for perceived speed.

domaines.fiche:
- Isolate the origin of a complex failure (multi-turn, multi-agent, non-deterministic): model output, harness, tools or data; refusals and grounding defects as failure classes.
- **Incident**: triage, mitigation, rollback, communication; then turn the incident into regression evaluations, monitoring coverage and a post-mortem.

questions.q: After a quality incident caused by a new prompt version, service is restored. Which step prevents it from happening again?

options.t: Add the incident's cases to the regression evaluations and to monitoring, and document a post-mortem

questions.why: an incident must become regression tests and better monitoring; that's what makes later releases safe.

questions.q: An agent's wrong answer cited a correct but outdated document returned by the search tool. Where does the failure originate?

options.t: In the data or retrieval (index not up to date), not in the model's reasoning
In the model, which must be replaced

questions.why: the model correctly used what it was given; the defect comes from the freshness of the retrieved data.

questions.q: During a platform provider outage, which mitigation is fastest if the architecture planned for it?

options.t: Switch to a planned fallback (another region, platform or model), respecting feature differences between platforms

questions.why: the surfaces (Anthropic API, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Foundry) don't all offer the same features; a cross-platform fallback must account for this parity.

domaines.fiche:
- Offline evaluations: golden sets, regression suites, behavior checks, **evaluation gates in CI/CD**, retrieval precision and grounding, release criteria; keeping the suite valid (contamination, saturation, coverage).
- **LLM-as-judge**: calibration on human labels, rubric, inter-rater agreement, judge drift.
- **Online quality**: traffic sampling, A/B tests, feedback loops, metrics suited to the task type.

questions.q: A team wants to automatically block merging a prompt change that lowers quality. Where should the evaluation go?

options.t: As a gate in the CI/CD pipeline: the regression suite must pass before merging

questions.why: success criteria and empirical evaluations serve as a quality gate before each change.

questions.q: An LLM judge serves as a release gate, but only agrees with human raters on a little over half the cases. What should you do?

options.t: Remove its gate authority, fix the rubric and recalibrate it on human labels until agreement is acceptable

questions.why: LLM grading is only worth something if it agrees with human judgment; until then, it must not decide alone.

questions.q: Every new version has passed the evaluation suite for months, and scores are close to the maximum. What risk does this signal?

options.t: A saturated suite that no longer tells versions apart: add harder cases representative of real traffic
The model should be changed immediately

questions.why: an evaluation suite must stay representative and discriminating; cases drawn from real traffic keep its coverage.

questions.q: For a field extraction task, which evaluation metric fits best?

options.t: An exact match with the expected value from a golden set

questions.why: you pick the metric by task type; for extraction, an exact comparison with the reference answer is simple and reliable.

domaines.fiche:
- Model and forecast costs; **model routing** and cascades within the Claude family; cache strategy and diagnostics; batch or real time; per-tenant budgets.
- **Latency**: tell time to first token apart from total latency; streaming, parallel tool execution, cache breakpoints, effort tuning.

questions.q: A service has a cache hit rate close to zero although every request starts with the same long system prompt. What is the most likely cause?

options.t: The cache breakpoint is placed after a variable part, so the prefix is never identical
The system prompt is too short

questions.why: the cache reuses an identical prefix up to the breakpoint; if it includes a variable part, nothing is ever reused.

questions.q: An application wants to reduce both perceived and total latency. Which techniques does Anthropic's documentation name?

options.t: Choose a faster model when it's enough, cut prompt and output tokens, and stream the response

questions.why: the latency page names model choice, reducing input and output tokens, and streaming.

domaines.fiche:
- **Layered** guardrails: input and output filtering, PII masking, **hook**-based policies, preventing destructive actions, sandboxing, approvals, refusal handling, **deterministic** enforcement for irreversible actions.
- Agent attack surface: prompt injection, tool and memory poisoning, exfiltration. The high-risk combination: **private data + untrusted input + external communication**. References: **OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications**, NIST AI RMF.
- **Identity**: workload identity federation instead of static API keys, secrets management, least privilege, auditing.

questions.q: An agent reads customer tickets, accesses the CRM and can send emails. A booby-trapped ticket makes it send another customer's data to an external address. An "ignore instructions in tickets" rule already exists. Which control closes the path?

options.t: A deterministic control outside the model: a recipient allow list or human approval on the email tool, and CRM access limited to the ticket's account
An even firmer instruction in the prompt

questions.why: the agent combines private data, untrusted input and an external channel; only a control enforced outside the model blocks exfiltration, whatever the injection.

questions.q: Production services use static, long-lived Claude API keys. Which alternative does the documentation recommend?
