Sharing the key across all repositories

questions.why: with OIDC, you no longer need to duplicate cloud credentials as long-lived secrets; the workflow requests a short-lived token.

questions.q: A team wants to prove where a published binary comes from (which workflow and commit built it). Which feature should it use?

options.t: Artifact attestations, which establish build provenance

questions.why: artifact attestations let you establish build provenance and verify it before deployment.

examens.mots_cles: github administration admin enterprise organisation, organization
examens.intro:
The **GitHub Administration** certification validates administering a GitHub Enterprise environment: identity and access, deployment and licensing, secure development and compliance, managing GitHub Actions, monitoring and optimizing usage.

The official guide dates its outline "July 2026" with no specific day: July 1 is a convention.

domaines.fiche:
- **Personal accounts** or **Enterprise Managed Users (EMU)**: with EMU, account lifecycle and authentication are managed from the company's **identity provider (IdP)**.
- **SAML SSO**, **2FA**, **SCIM** provisioning; **team synchronization**: connect organization teams to **IdP groups**.
- Organization and repository roles, enterprise teams, access audits; **rulesets** on top of branch protection rules.

questions.q: A company wants to create, deactivate and authenticate its employees' GitHub accounts entirely from its identity provider. Which option should it choose?

options.t: Personal accounts invited to the organization

questions.why: with Enterprise Managed Users, the company manages the lifecycle and authentication of users from its IdP.

questions.q: The members of a GitHub team must automatically follow membership of a group in the company's IdP. Which feature should you use?
questions.why: team synchronization lets you connect organization teams to IdP groups.

questions.q: A company wants access to GitHub to go through its IdP's authentication (Entra ID, Okta…). Which mechanism should it configure?
questions.why: SAML lets you delegate authentication to a company identity provider.

questions.q: A repository already has branch protection rules; the administrator adds a ruleset on the same branch. What happens?

options.t: Both apply together: all applicable rules are enforced
The ruleset replaces and cancels the branch protection

questions.why: rulesets and branch protection rules work together; all applicable rules are enforced.

questions.q: A contractor must be able to manage a repository's issues and pull requests without pushing code. Which repository role should they get?
questions.why: Triage is designed for managing issues, discussions and pull requests without write access.

questions.q: An administrator wants to know who changed an organization's security settings last month. Where should they look?
questions.why: the audit log records the actions taken in the enterprise and its organizations.

domaines.fiche:
- Tell apart what the administrator handles and what belongs to **GitHub Support**; generate **diagnostic files and support bundles** (GHES).
- Set standards: workflows, branches, reviews, releases.
- Deployment scenarios: **GHEC with EMU**, **GHEC with data residency + EMU**, **GHEC with personal accounts**, **GitHub Enterprise Server** (self-hosted).
- Licensing, billing, usage tracking.

questions.q: A GitHub Enterprise Server administrator must send GitHub Support the information needed to analyze an incident. What should she provide?

options.t: Diagnostic files or a support bundle
A screenshot of the home page
The list of the repositories' stars

questions.why: GitHub Enterprise Server lets you generate diagnostic files and support bundles to give to Support.

questions.q: A regulated company must store its GitHub data in a specific geographic region while using GitHub's cloud. Which option should it look at?

options.t: GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency

questions.why: GitHub Enterprise Cloud offers a data residency option.

questions.q: An organization wants to host GitHub in its own datacenter, on its own infrastructure. Which product fits?
questions.why: GitHub Enterprise Server is the self-hosted version, which the company runs on its own infrastructure.

questions.q: To standardize practices, the administrator wants every main branch to require a review and passing checks before merging, across the whole organization. Which tool should they use?
questions.why: rulesets define protection rules applied to branches, including at scale.

domaines.nom: Enable secure software development and ensure compliance
domaines.fiche:
- Enterprise and organization policies, security posture, **audit log**.
- Repository security: vulnerability alerts, **secret scanning**, **CodeQL**, **Dependabot**, security advisories, response plan.
- **API access**: **fine-grained** (recommended) or **classic** PATs; REST API rate limits: **5,000 requests/hour** for a user, **15,000** for a GitHub App owned by a GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization; **GitHub Apps** (fine-grained permissions, can act without a user) or **OAuth Apps**; approving or denying applications.
- **IP allow list** to restrict access to resources.

questions.q: A developer must create a token for a script that reads a single repository. Which type of token does GitHub recommend?

options.t: A fine-grained personal access token, limited to that repository and the needed permissions
A classic personal access token with full rights

questions.why: GitHub recommends fine-grained personal access tokens over classic tokens whenever possible.

questions.q: An integration makes many REST API calls with a PAT and hits the limit. Which limit applies, and which alternative offers more capacity in GitHub Enterprise Cloud?

options.t: 5,000 requests per hour for the user; a GitHub App owned by a GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization has a higher limit (15,000 per hour)
100 requests per day, with no alternative
The limit depends on the repository's stars

questions.why: the personal limit is 5,000 requests per hour; a GitHub App owned by a GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization has a limit of 15,000 requests per hour.

questions.q: Why does GitHub generally recommend a GitHub App over an OAuth App for an integration?

options.t: GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions and can act independently of a user
OAuth Apps are free and GitHub Apps are paid
GitHub Apps have no rate limit

questions.why: GitHub Apps are preferred because they use fine-grained permissions, give more control over which repositories they can access and can act without a user.

questions.q: An automation must keep working even when the employee who set it up leaves the company. Which type of integration should you choose?

options.t: A GitHub App, which can act independently of a user
An OAuth App tied to the employee's account

questions.why: a GitHub App can act independently of a user; it keeps working after the person who installed it leaves.

questions.q: The organization wants its resources to be reachable only from the company network. What should it configure?
questions.why: the IP allow list determines whether users or apps can access protected resources through the web interface, the API or Git.

questions.q: A developer pushes an API key to a repository by mistake. Which feature could have blocked this push?
questions.why: push protection prevents hard-coded credentials, such as secrets or tokens, from being pushed to the repository.

questions.q: Vulnerable dependencies must be fixed automatically through update pull requests. Which feature should you turn on?
questions.why: Dependabot can fix vulnerable dependencies by opening security update pull requests.

questions.q: An administrator must scan the repositories' code for vulnerabilities with the tool maintained by GitHub. Which one?
questions.why: code scanning can use CodeQL, maintained by GitHub, or a third-party tool.

domaines.fiche:
- Reusing actions and workflows across the enterprise; Actions **policies** (allowed actions).
- Hosted or self-hosted **runners**; **runner groups**; IP lists and networking, including **Azure private networking** for GitHub-hosted runners; monitoring and troubleshooting.
- **Encrypted secrets**: scope and access, organization and repository levels, third-party vaults.

questions.q: GitHub-hosted runners must reach resources in the company's private Azure virtual network. Which feature should you use?

options.t: Azure private networking for GitHub-hosted runners
A public runner with no configuration

questions.why: the enterprise can configure Azure private networking for its GitHub-hosted runners.

questions.q: Only the data platform teams must be able to use certain self-hosted runners. What should you configure?

options.t: A runner group limited to the relevant organizations and repositories

questions.why: runner groups control which organizations and repositories can use runners.

questions.q: A deployment token must be available to several repositories of the organization, but not all. How should you store it?

options.t: As an organization secret, with access limited to selected repositories
In plain text in each workflow
In a file in the repository

questions.why: organization secrets can be limited to chosen repositories.

questions.q: The company wants repositories to use only verified or approved actions. Where do you configure this?

options.t: In the enterprise or organization GitHub Actions policies

questions.why: Actions policies let you limit the allowed actions and workflows.

questions.q: A reusable deployment workflow must be shared across the whole company and maintained in one place. Which approach?

options.t: A reusable workflow stored in a repository accessible to the others, called by their workflows
Copy the file into each repository

questions.why: reusable workflows centralize logic called by other workflows.

questions.q: Rather than storing long-lived cloud secrets in GitHub, which approach should you recommend for deployments?

options.t: A shared key in the README
A classic PAT with full rights

questions.why: with OIDC, you no longer need to store long-lived cloud credentials as GitHub secrets.

questions.q: A self-hosted runner is used by public repositories. What risk does this present?

options.t: Untrusted code from pull requests could run on the machine; avoid self-hosted runners for public repositories

questions.why: the security documentation recommends not using self-hosted runners with public repositories, because anyone can get code to run on them.

domaines.fiche:
- Analyze the **audit log** and API usage; tell apart the administrator's role and Support's; generate diagnostics.
- Assess adoption and underused features.
- Read **usage reports** for metered products (Actions, Packages, Codespaces…); optimize licenses and resources.

questions.q: The CFO notices a rise in the GitHub bill. Where does the administrator find the consumption details (Actions minutes, storage, etc.)?

options.t: In the enterprise usage and billing reports

questions.why: usage reports detail the consumption of metered products.

questions.q: Dozens of licenses are assigned to accounts inactive for six months. Which optimization action should you recommend?

options.t: Identify inactive members (audit log, reports) and reclaim their licenses

questions.why: tracking activity and license consumption lets you reclaim the ones that aren't used.

questions.q: A GitHub Enterprise Server performance issue is beyond the internal team's skills. What process should you follow?

options.t: Open a ticket with GitHub Support, attaching diagnostic files or a support bundle

questions.why: GitHub Support analyzes incidents from the diagnostic files and support bundles provided by the administrator.

questions.q: An administrator wants to spot the integrations that consume the most API calls. What should they monitor?

options.t: API usage and rate limits (rate limit headers, audit log)

questions.why: REST API rate limits are tracked per user or app, which lets you identify heavy consumers.

questions.q: Which task belongs to the organization administrator rather than GitHub Support?

options.t: Managing the organization's members, teams, roles and policies
Fixing an outage of the github.com infrastructure

questions.why: administrators manage members, teams, roles and policies; issues with the platform itself belong to GitHub Support.

examens.mots_cles: github advanced security ghas sécurité secret protection code security codeql dependabot, security
examens.intro:
The **GitHub Advanced Security** certification validates securing code with GitHub's security suites: **Secret Protection** (formerly secret scanning), **Supply Chain Security** (formerly Dependabot and Dependency Review), **Code Security** (formerly code scanning with CodeQL), security operations and administration at scale.

The official guide dates its outline "July 2026" with no specific day: July 1 is a convention. It uses the new product names; the old names are still common in the documentation.

domaines.fiche:
- Three suites: **GitHub Secret Protection** (secret leaks), **GitHub Code Security** (code analysis, dependency review…), **Supply Chain Security** (dependencies).
- Free features for public repositories, and paid suites for enterprise private repositories.
- **Security overview**: an overview of risks and coverage.
- Secure SDLC: **prevention first** (push protection, dependency review before merge) rather than blocking checks at the end of the chain; **security campaigns** to burn down the backlog.
- Alert management: roles, responsibilities, consequences of dismissing an alert.

questions.q: A team wants an overview of alerts and of security feature enablement across all the organization's repositories. Which tool should it use?
questions.why: the security overview gives a consolidated view of risks and security feature coverage.

questions.q: What are GitHub's paid security suites for private repositories?

options.t: GitHub Secret Protection and GitHub Code Security

questions.why: the documentation presents the features available with GitHub Secret Protection and with GitHub Code Security.

questions.q: A security team has 2,000 old alerts and wants to burn them down with developers, in targeted batches. Which feature should it use?
questions.why: security campaigns let you fix alerts at scale by working with developers to reduce the security backlog.

questions.q: Which approach matches a "prevention first" strategy?

options.t: Blocking secrets at push time and checking dependencies before merge
Only scanning production code once a year
Waiting for an incident to react
Ignoring both low- and high-severity alerts

questions.why: push protection keeps secrets out of the repository instead of alerting afterwards; dependency review acts on every pull request.

questions.q: What does dependency review provide in a pull request?

options.t: A view of dependency changes and their security impact, with a diff in the Files Changed tab
An AI summary of the commits

questions.why: dependency review shows dependency changes and their security impact on every pull request.

questions.q: A developer dismisses a secret alert as a "false positive" without checking. What is the risk?

options.t: A real exposed secret stays exploitable; a dismissal must be justified and verified

questions.why: dismissing an alert removes it from tracking; if the secret is real and active, it stays exploitable. Validity checks help tell whether a secret is still active.

domaines.fiche:
- Turn it on at repository and organization level; differences between public and private repositories.
- **Push protection**: blocks secrets **before** they enter the repository; bypasses generate alerts.
- **Validity checks**: check whether a detected secret is **still active**, to prioritize.
- Alert lifecycle (creation, status, dismissal) and remediation: **revoke and rotate the secret**.
- **Delegated bypass**: bypassing push protection goes through **review and approval**.
- Alert recipients, exclusions, **custom patterns**.

questions.q: How does push protection protect a repository?

options.t: It prevents hard-coded credentials from being pushed, instead of alerting after the leak

questions.why: push protection prevents hard-coded secrets and tokens from being pushed; it acts before the leak rather than after.

questions.q: An alert reports an exposed cloud token. How do you prioritize quickly?

options.t: Use validity checks to know whether the secret is still active
Wait until the end of the month

questions.why: validity checks verify whether a detected secret is still active, so you handle exploitable secrets first.

questions.q: An active secret was pushed into a repository's history. What is the first remediation action?

options.t: Revoke and rotate the secret with the relevant service, then handle the history
Only delete the line in the last commit
Make the repository private and do nothing else

questions.why: an exposed secret must be treated as compromised; removing it from the code isn't enough, it must be revoked.

questions.q: An organization wants every push protection bypass to be reviewed and approved by the security team. What should it configure?
questions.why: delegated bypass introduces a review of push protection bypass requests.

questions.q: The company uses an internal token format that GitHub doesn't know. How do you get it detected?

options.t: Define a secret scanning custom pattern
Add the token to the README

questions.why: custom patterns let you detect secret formats specific to the organization.

questions.q: A developer bypasses push protection to push a file. What happens?

options.t: The bypass generates a secret scanning alert, visible to the security team
The developer's account is suspended automatically

questions.why: push protection generates alerts for bypasses, so they can be tracked.

domaines.nom: Configure and use Supply Chain Security
domaines.fiche:
- **Dependency graph**; **SBOM** exportable in the standard **SPDX** format.
- **Dependabot alerts**: created among other things when a vulnerability is added to the **GitHub Advisory Database**; prioritization with severity and **EPSS** scores.
- **Dependabot security updates** (fix pull requests) and **version updates** (`dependabot.yml` file, grouped updates).
- **Dependency review** before merge (licenses, compliance).

questions.q: A customer requires the list of a product's software components in a standard format. What should you provide?

options.t: An SBOM exported from the dependency graph, in SPDX format

questions.why: GitHub lets you export an SBOM in the standard SPDX format.

questions.q: Which metric, shown alongside severity, helps prioritize Dependabot alerts by likelihood of exploitation?

options.t: The EPSS (Exploit Prediction Scoring System) score

questions.why: Dependabot alerts show severity, EPSS scores and other information to help prioritize.

questions.q: How do you turn on regular dependency version updates by Dependabot?

options.t: By adding a dependabot.yml configuration file to the repository
They are always on with no configuration

questions.why: version updates are turned on by adding a dependabot.yml file to the repository.

questions.q: When does Dependabot create a new alert on a repository?

options.t: For example when a new vulnerability is added to the GitHub Advisory Database and affects one of the repository's dependencies
On every commit, whatever its content
Only when the repository is created

questions.why: one of the triggers of Dependabot alerts is a new vulnerability being added to the GitHub Advisory Database.

questions.q: A pull request adds a vulnerable dependency. Which check flags it before the merge?

options.t: Dependency review in the pull request

questions.why: dependency review shows dependency changes and their security impact on every pull request.

domaines.fiche:
- **Code scanning** with **CodeQL** (maintained by GitHub) or a third-party tool that produces **SARIF** (an open format).
- **Default setup**: the simplest, creates a configuration automatically, customizable at scale with no workflow file. **Advanced setup**: a custom workflow.
- Analyzing results (data flow), alert lifecycle, **Copilot Autofix** (a fix suggestion for an alert, which you review and apply), dismissal and severity.

questions.q: A team already uses a third-party static analysis tool and wants to see its results in GitHub. What should it do?

options.t: Upload its results in SARIF format to code scanning
Copy the results into the README

questions.why: code scanning accepts third-party tools that produce SARIF data, an open standard.

questions.q: An organization wants to turn on CodeQL quickly across hundreds of repositories, without writing or maintaining a workflow file. Which setup should it choose?
questions.why: default setup creates a configuration automatically, customizable across the organization without creating or maintaining a workflow.

questions.q: A developer wants a suggested fix for a specific CodeQL alert, which they'll review before applying. Which feature should they use?
questions.why: Copilot Autofix suggests a code change for an alert, which the developer reviews and applies themselves.

questions.q: When should you prefer the advanced CodeQL setup?

options.t: When you need a custom workflow (specific build steps, particular queries or frequency)

questions.why: GitHub offers a default setup and an advanced setup depending on your needs; advanced lets you customize the workflow.

domaines.fiche:
- **CVE**, **CWE**, **GitHub Security Advisories**; end-to-end remediation flow.
- Prioritizing: severity, EPSS, remediation rules; campaigns and bulk alert management; documenting dismissals.
- Customizing CodeQL (query suites) to the risk profile.
- Security roles, delegated exceptions, alert ownership; **shift left**: push protection, dependency analysis and analysis before merge.

questions.q: A public vulnerability is referenced by a CVE identifier. Where do you find the matching advisory for dependency ecosystems, used by Dependabot?
questions.why: the GitHub Advisory Database gathers security advisories, with a link to the CVE record for those from the National Vulnerability Database.

questions.q: The security team has hundreds of alerts of the same type across several repositories. How should remediation be organized?

options.t: Launch a targeted security campaign, tracked with the development teams
Dismiss all alerts in bulk without justification

questions.why: security campaigns let you fix alerts at scale in collaboration with developers.

questions.q: Which set of practices illustrates "shifting security left"?

options.t: Push protection, dependency analysis and code analysis before merge
A yearly audit in production only

questions.why: the outline names early prevention: push protection, dependency analysis and analysis before merge.

questions.q: Why document the reason for dismissing a security alert?

options.t: To keep an auditable record of decisions and be able to revisit them
To increase the number of alerts

questions.why: dismissed alerts leave tracking; a documented justification enables governance and review.

domaines.fiche:
- Turn on the suites at enterprise, organization and repository level; differences between GitHub Enterprise Cloud and GitHub Enterprise Server.
- Default **security configurations** and inheritance; turn on CodeQL, Secret Protection and Supply Chain Security at scale.
- Policies and rulesets, enforcement limits, bypass permissions, roles (administrator, **security manager**, developer), alert dismissal rights.
- APIs and automation for configuration at scale.

questions.q: A company wants to turn on the same security features for all its new repositories, with no manual setup. What should it define?

options.t: A default security configuration applied to the organization's repositories

questions.why: security configurations let you apply a set of features to many repositories, including by default to new ones.

questions.q: Who should be able to dismiss a critical code scanning alert in a well-governed organization?

options.t: Authorized people (for example security managers), according to configured permissions

questions.why: the outline covers configuring alert management and dismissal permissions by role.

questions.q: A team wants to see where security features aren't yet turned on in the organization. Which tool should it use?

options.t: The security overview, which shows feature coverage

questions.why: the security overview presents risks and security feature coverage across repositories.

questions.q: To turn on security features across thousands of repositories in a repeatable way, which approach should you favor?

options.t: A manual click on each repository

questions.why: the outline covers APIs and automation methods for security configuration at scale, in addition to security configurations.

questions.q: A company uses both GitHub Enterprise Cloud and GitHub Enterprise Server. What should the administrator check before rolling out a security feature?

options.t: Its availability and differences by platform and version

questions.why: feature availability differs between GitHub Enterprise Cloud and GitHub Enterprise Server; the documentation shows what is available with each product.

examens.intro: The entry-level Power Platform exam: the business value of each service, Dataverse, administration, and what Power Apps, Power Automate and Copilot Studio agents can do. No coding required. The July 2026 outline gives AI a large place: Plans, the "vibe" experience, code apps, agents, Microsoft Agent 365.

domaines.nom: Describe the business value of Power Platform
domaines.fiche:
- **Power Apps**: business apps in low-code (canvas, model-driven) and in code (code apps).
- **Power Automate**: process automation, with cloud flows (APIs and connectors) and desktop flows (RPA on existing interfaces).
- **Dataverse**: structured storage for business data, with built-in security, business logic and metadata.
- **Connectors**: more than 1,000 ready-to-use services (Microsoft 365, SQL, Salesforce…), plus custom connectors.
- **Power Pages**: secure websites for **external** users (customers, partners).
- **Copilot Studio**: building conversational and autonomous agents.
- **Generative AI**: describe a table, an app, a flow or a complete solution (Plans) in natural language instead of building everything by hand.

questions.q: A nonprofit wants a portal where its members (external to the organization) view and update their information stored in Dataverse. Which Power Platform service meets this need?

options.t: A canvas app shared with each member

questions.why: Power Pages is used to build secure websites for external users, with Dataverse data.

questions.q: What is the main benefit of connectors in Power Platform?

options.t: They replace Dataverse for storing data
They let apps, flows and agents use the data and actions of other services without writing an integration
They are only used to import Excel files
They encrypt data between two environments

questions.why: a connector wraps a service's API and exposes it as triggers and actions that can be used directly.

domaines.fiche:
**Dataverse**
- Data in **tables** (standard, custom), typed **columns** and **relationships**: one-to-many (1:N), many-to-one (N:1), many-to-many (N:N).
- Compared with a classic database: built-in role-based security, business logic (business rules, Power Fx formulas, plug-ins), auditing, rich metadata, ready-to-use forms and views.
- **Forms** to display and edit one record, **views** to list filtered records.
- No-code business logic: **business rules**, Power Fx **formula columns**.
- Copilot lets you describe a table in natural language to generate its columns and relationships.

**Administration and governance**
- An **environment** is a container for apps, flows, agents and data, tied to a tenant and a geography. It has **zero or one** Dataverse database.
- Environment types: Production, Sandbox, Developer, Trial, Default, Dataverse for Teams.
- Security: environment roles (Environment Admin, Environment Maker), Dataverse security roles, business units, teams. **Data policies (DLP)** classify connectors to prevent certain combinations.
- Monitoring: analytics and Monitor in the Power Platform admin center.
- **ALM**: solutions, and Power Platform **pipelines** to deploy from Dev to Test then Prod without external tooling.

questions.q: How many Dataverse databases can a Power Platform environment contain?

options.t: As many as the number of licenses

questions.why: each environment can have zero or one Dataverse database; you separate Dev, Test and Prod by creating several environments.

questions.q: A "Project" table must be linked to several "Skills", and each skill to several projects. Which type of relationship do you need?
questions.why: each side can be associated with several records on the other side: that's a many-to-many relationship.

questions.q: Which Dataverse element lists several records of a table with a filter and chosen columns?
questions.why: a view defines the columns, sort and filter of a list of records; a form displays a single record.

questions.q: An administrator wants to prevent a flow from combining a business connector (Dataverse) with a public social media connector. Which tool do they use?
questions.why: data policies classify connectors (Business, Non-Business, Blocked) and forbid mixing groups in the same app or flow.

questions.q: What are the two built-in roles at the level of an environment without a Dataverse database?

options.t: Global Admin and Power Platform Admin

questions.why: an environment has two built-in roles, Environment Admin and Environment Maker; with Dataverse, Dataverse security roles apply.

questions.q: A team of makers wants to deploy its solution from Dev to Test then Prod, directly from Power Apps, without setting up Azure DevOps. Which feature fits?
questions.why: pipelines bring ALM and automated deployment into the product, set up by an administrator and usable by makers.

questions.q: Which Dataverse mechanism applies, with no code, logic such as "make the Discount column required if the amount exceeds €10,000"?
questions.why: business rules apply conditions and actions (required, visible, value, error message) on a table without code.

domaines.nom: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
domaines.fiche:
- **Canvas app**: you start from the interface; full control of the layout, many data sources through connectors; Power Fx formulas.
- **Model-driven app**: you start from Dataverse data; the interface (forms, views, dashboards) is generated and responsive. Ideal for rich business processes.
- **Plans (Plan designer)**: you describe the need in natural language, with images if needed, and Copilot proposes a complete solution: Dataverse tables, canvas and model-driven apps, Power Pages sites, flows and agents. Requires a Dataverse database.
- **Code apps**: web apps written in an IDE (VS Code) with React, Vue…, hosted by Power Platform, with Entra authentication, connectors callable from JavaScript and policy enforcement (DLP, Conditional Access).
- **"Vibe" experience** (preview): an AI-native platform that generates requirements, data model and a code app from a description.
- With Copilot, you create a canvas app or a model-driven app by describing what you want.

questions.q: A field team wants a highly customized mobile app, with a precise layout, that reads a SharePoint list and a SQL table. Which type of app should it choose?

options.t: A plan generated by Plan designer only

questions.why: a canvas app gives control of the layout and connects to many sources through connectors; a model-driven app is built on Dataverse.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a model-driven app?

options.t: It is built pixel by pixel from a blank screen
Its interface is generated from Dataverse components (forms, views, dashboards) and adapts to the screen
It can only display SharePoint data
It must be written in React

questions.why: a model-driven app starts from Dataverse data and components; its layout is determined by those components and it is responsive.

questions.q: A business manager describes their onboarding process in natural language and attaches a screenshot of the old tool. They want to get the tables, apps and flows in one go. Which feature are they using?
questions.why: Plans generates a complete solution (Dataverse tables, apps, sites, flows, agents) from a description and images.

questions.q: Which environment prerequisite is required to use Plans in Power Apps?

options.t: A Dataverse database in the environment

questions.why: the documentation requires a Dataverse database; without one, users are redirected to their Developer environment if they're entitled to it.

questions.q: A developer wants to write a business app in React in Visual Studio Code, while benefiting from Power Platform's Entra authentication, connectors and DLP policies. Which option fits?

options.t: A canvas app with Power Fx components
A Power Pages site in code-only mode

questions.why: code apps are developed in an IDE with frameworks such as React or Vue and run on the managed Power Apps platform.

questions.q: Which tools does the documentation ask you to install to build code apps?

options.t: Visual Studio and the .NET SDK only
An IDE, Node.js, Git and the Power Apps CLI
Power BI Desktop and a gateway
None: everything happens in the browser

questions.why: the listed prerequisites are an IDE, Node.js (LTS), Git and the Power Apps CLI.

questions.q: Which description fits the new Power Apps "vibe" experience?

options.t: A visual theme for canvas apps
An AI-native platform that generates requirements, data and an app with generated code, from a description

questions.why: the documentation presents it as an AI-native platform that produces requirements, data model and a complete code app; it is in preview.

domaines.nom: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
domaines.fiche:
- **Cloud flows**: run in the cloud through connectors. Three ways to start: **automated** (an event), **instant** (a button, an app) and **scheduled** (a recurrence).
- **Desktop flows**: robotic process automation (RPA) of desktop or web apps with no API, in **attended** (user present) or **unattended** (machine with no open session) mode.
- Common cases: approvals, Teams notifications, processing Outlook emails, SharePoint files, Forms responses, AI document processing.
- A flow = a **trigger** + **actions**.
- Copilot creates or edits a flow from a natural language description; there is also AI help for desktop flows.

questions.q: A flow must run every Monday at 8 a.m. to send a report. Which type of cloud flow do you need?
questions.why: a scheduled flow starts on a recurrence (day, time); an automated flow reacts to an event, an instant flow to a manual action.

questions.q: A company must enter data every day into an old desktop application that has no API. Which Power Automate solution fits?

options.t: A cloud flow with the Dataverse connector

questions.why: desktop flows automate the interfaces of desktop and web applications when no API is available.

questions.q: In a cloud flow "When an email arrives in Outlook, save the attachment to SharePoint", what is the role of "When an email arrives"?
questions.why: every flow starts with a trigger, the event that starts it; the following steps are actions.

questions.q: A manager must approve every expense report above €500 from Teams or Outlook. Which Power Automate feature should be used?
questions.why: the approval action sends the request to the approver, who responds from Teams, Outlook or the approvals center, and the flow continues based on the response.

questions.q: What is the difference between an attended and an unattended desktop flow?

options.t: Attended runs in the cloud, unattended on a workstation
Attended runs with a signed-in, present user; unattended runs on a machine without human intervention
Attended is free, unattended only exists in preview

questions.why: attended mode assists an active user in their session; unattended mode runs the automation with nobody in front of the machine.

questions.q: A maker types "When a row is added to my SharePoint list, post a message in the team's Teams channel". What does Copilot in Power Automate do?

options.t: It opens a ticket with Microsoft support
It proposes a flow with the matching trigger and actions, which the maker can adjust
It installs a desktop flow on the workstation

questions.why: Copilot in Power Automate generates a cloud flow from a natural language description, then helps edit it.

questions.q: Which connector is best suited to start a flow when someone answers a questionnaire?

options.t: Microsoft Forms, "When a new response is submitted" trigger

questions.why: the Microsoft Forms connector provides a trigger on the submission of a new response.

domaines.fiche:
- **Use cases**: HR or IT support, customer FAQ, appointment booking assistant, agents that act autonomously on events.
- **Topics**: conversation paths (triggering, questions, conditions, messages). There are system topics (greeting, fallback, escalation…).
- **Knowledge**: public websites, SharePoint, uploaded files, Dataverse… The agent draws its generated answers from it.
- **Tools**: connectors, agent flows, prompts, and **MCP** servers (Copilot Studio supports MCP *tools* and *resources*).
- **Channels**: Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot, website, mobile apps, messaging networks. Publishing updates all connected channels. The **Authenticate with Microsoft** (Entra ID) option is on by default.
- **Microsoft Agent 365**: an observability platform for all the organization's agents (registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center). Four pillars: management, governance, security, business value.
- **Monitoring**: usage and adoption analytics in Copilot Studio.
- **Agent evaluation**: test sets that simulate conversations and measure accuracy, relevance and quality. Four safety evaluators are added: hateful and unfair speech, sexual content, violence, self-harm.

questions.q: In Copilot Studio, what is a topic for?

options.t: Defining a conversation path: how the agent is triggered, what it asks and answers
Assigning a license to the agent

questions.why: a topic describes a portion of conversation, with its trigger and its nodes (questions, messages, conditions, actions).

questions.q: An HR agent must answer questions about the leave policy, published on a SharePoint site. What should be added to the agent?

options.t: The SharePoint site as a knowledge source

questions.why: adding SharePoint as knowledge lets the agent generate answers from that content, without writing one topic per question.

questions.q: A Copilot Studio agent connects to an MCP server. Which MCP elements does Copilot Studio currently support?
questions.why: the documentation states that Copilot Studio currently supports MCP tools and resources.

questions.q: A maker changes their agent, already published in Teams and on the website, but users don't see the change. Why?

options.t: The agent must be republished; publishing updates all connected channels
Each channel must be deleted and recreated

questions.why: changes only become visible after a new publish, which applies to all connected channels.

questions.q: Which authentication option is on by default for a new Copilot Studio agent?

options.t: Authenticate manually with a third-party OAuth provider

questions.why: "Authenticate with Microsoft" is on by default and uses Entra ID for Teams, Power Apps and Microsoft Copilot.

questions.q: What is the role of Microsoft Agent 365?

options.t: A new tool for writing topics
An observability platform that gives a single view of the organization's agents, Microsoft or third-party, for management, governance, security and business value
A license that replaces Copilot Studio

questions.why: Agent 365 brings agents together in a registry and rests on four pillars: management, governance, security, business value.

questions.q: Before putting an agent into production, a team wants to automatically test dozens of questions and measure the accuracy and relevance of the answers. Which feature does it use?

options.t: Agent evaluation (test sets) in Copilot Studio

questions.why: agent evaluation generates test cases that simulate conversations and measures accuracy, relevance and quality, plus safety evaluators.

examens.intro: AB-400 replaces PL-400, retired on October 30, 2026 ([source](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/skills-hub-blog/updates-to-azure-cosmos-db-and-power-platform-developer-certifications/4528353)). It keeps the Dataverse developer foundation (plug-ins, Client API, PCF, Web API, integrations), plus what's new: code apps, generative pages, Microsoft Foundry and Copilot Studio agents, MCP, Work IQ, background operations.

domaines.fiche:
**Architecture**
- Put logic in the right place: business rule or Power Fx (simple, no code), client script (form experience), plug-in (server, synchronous, transactional), flow (asynchronous, integrations), Azure (long or heavy processing).
- **Deterministic** (rules, plug-ins, formulas) when the result must always be the same. **Non-deterministic** (generative AI, agents) when some interpretation is acceptable.
- Tables: **standard** (relational, transactional), **virtual** (external data with no copy), **elastic** (Azure Cosmos DB, large volumes and load spikes, no cross-table transactions), or a plain **connector**.
- Interface: code apps, **generative pages** (model-driven app pages generated in React from a description), PCF, web resources, interactive agents, MCP widgets.
- Security: managed environments, data policies, roles, teams, business units, record sharing.

**ALM**
- **Solution layers**: managed solutions stack up, the active unmanaged layer sits on top and wins.
- **Environment variables**: values specific to each environment (URL, ID, Azure Key Vault secret) without changing the solution.
- Power Platform **pipelines** (extensible) and **Power Platform Build Tools** (Azure DevOps) or GitHub Actions for CI/CD.
- Handle solution **dependencies** before importing.

questions.q: An integration must store millions of IoT events per day, with a schema that changes often and unpredictable load spikes. No cross-table transaction is needed. Which type of Dataverse table should you choose?
questions.why: elastic tables are built on Azure Cosmos DB and scale out horizontally; they suit large volumes and changing schemas, but not cross-table transactions.

questions.q: Customer orders stay in an external SQL ERP. Users want to see them in a model-driven app as a Dataverse table, without copying the data. Which option?

options.t: An elastic table synchronized every night

questions.why: a virtual table shows external data as a Dataverse table, without replicating it.

questions.q: A partner API's URL differs between Dev, Test and Prod. How do you avoid changing the solution on every deployment?

options.t: Hard-code the URL in the plug-in and recompile per environment
Use an environment variable whose value is set in each environment
Store the URL in a column of an account record

questions.why: environment variables separate the definition (in the solution) from the value (specific to each environment), including secrets through Azure Key Vault.

questions.q: After importing a managed solution, a form doesn't show the expected change. The form had been edited directly in Prod. What is the most likely cause?

options.t: The active unmanaged layer, above the managed layers, wins
The browser cache always blocks imports
A plug-in is needed to activate the form

questions.why: unmanaged customizations form the active layer, on top; they hide the changes of managed solutions imported below.

questions.q: A team wants to automate export, checking and import of its solutions from Azure DevOps. Which Microsoft tooling does it use?

options.t: Solution Packager alone, run by hand

questions.why: Power Platform Build Tools provide Azure DevOps tasks to export, check, pack and import solutions in CI/CD pipelines.

domaines.fiche:
**Client API (model-driven app scripts)**
- Getting the context: `executionContext.getFormContext()` (stop using the deprecated `Xrm.Page`). Check "Pass execution context" when registering the handler.
- Registering handlers: in the form designer (OnLoad, OnSave, OnChange) or in code (`addOnChange`).
- Data: `Xrm.WebApi.retrieveRecord`, `retrieveMultipleRecords`, `createRecord`, `updateRecord`.
- Interface: `formContext.ui.setFormNotification`, `Xrm.App.addGlobalNotification`, `Xrm.Navigation.openConfirmDialog`, `openAlertDialog`, `navigateTo`.
- Modern commands: buttons defined in **Power Fx** or **JavaScript** in the command designer.

**PCF (Power Apps component framework)**
- Lifecycle: `init` (once), `updateView` (on every data or size change), `getOutputs` (called after `notifyOutputChanged`), `destroy`.
- `ControlManifest.Input.xml` manifest: properties (`bound`, `input`, `output`), resources, and `<uses-feature>` to enable Device, Utility or WebAPI.
- `pac pcf push` to test quickly; a solution to deploy properly.

**Code apps**
- React, Vue… apps developed locally, hosted on Power Platform: connections, Dataverse tables, flows, Copilot Studio agents, environment variables.
- Deployment with the CLI; **CSP** to configure; monitoring with **Application Insights** and Monitor.

questions.q: In an OnChange handler of a model-driven form, what is the recommended way to access the form's columns?
questions.why: `Xrm.Page` is deprecated; you get the formContext from the execution context passed to the handler.

questions.q: A script must read the last 10 open opportunities of the displayed account, without reloading the form. Which method should it use?
questions.why: `retrieveMultipleRecords` queries the Dataverse Web API with OData options ($select, $filter, $top…) and returns a promise.

questions.q: Before saving, the user must confirm an exceptional discount through a dialog with OK and Cancel. Which method fits?
questions.why: `openConfirmDialog` shows a message with two buttons and returns the user's choice; `openAlertDialog` has only one button.

questions.q: A PCF component must redraw when the bound column's value changes or when the container size changes. Which method does the framework call in these cases?
questions.why: `updateView` is called when a property value, metadata or the container size changes; `init` is called only once.

questions.q: A PCF component changes the entered value and must send it back to the bound column. Which sequence is correct?
questions.why: the component signals a change with `notifyOutputChanged`; the framework then calls `getOutputs` to read the new values.

questions.q: A PCF component must take a photo with the device. What must be declared in the manifest?

options.t: Nothing, the Device API is always available

questions.why: Device, Utility and WebAPI features must be declared with `<uses-feature>` in the manifest before they can be used.

questions.q: A maker wants to add to a model-driven app a tracking page described in natural language, using two Dataverse tables, with a screenshot as a model. Which feature generates this page?

options.t: A generative page, which produces React code from the description
An HTML web resource written by hand

questions.why: generative pages are created by the app agent from a description, Dataverse tables and an optional image; the system generates the page's React code.

questions.q: In the modern command designer, which languages can you use to define a button's action?
questions.why: modern commands accept a Power Fx action or a call to a JavaScript library.

domaines.fiche:
**Plug-ins**
- Pipeline stages: **PreValidation** (10, outside the transaction, before security checks), **PreOperation** (20, inside the transaction, you can change the Target), **MainOperation** (30, the operation itself, reserved for custom APIs), **PostOperation** (40, inside the transaction when synchronous).
- Context: `IPluginExecutionContext` (Target, InputParameters, Depth…), `IOrganizationServiceFactory`, `ITracingService`.
- **Images**: pre-image (not on Create) and post-image (not on Delete), to avoid a re-read.
- Maximum plug-in timeout: **2 minutes**. Asynchronous mode doesn't give more time.
- **Custom API**: a custom business message (function or action, bound to a table or not), implemented by a plug-in.
- **Managed identity** (version 2 recommended): the plug-in reaches Azure resources with no secret.

**Platform APIs**
- Web API (OData v4) and Organization service (.NET SDK), Python SDK.
- **Service protection limits**: when exceeded, a 429 error with a `Retry-After` header to respect.
- Bulk operations: `CreateMultiple`, `UpdateMultiple`, `UpsertMultiple`.
- Optimistic concurrency with `If-Match` and the ETag.
- **Background operations** (preview): run a custom API asynchronously, with a callback URL or the `OnBackgroundOperationComplete` event.

**Azure Functions**: long processing (Durable Functions), scheduled or event-based triggers, managed identity authentication.

**Flows**: expressions, error handling with **Configure run after** and **Scopes** (try/catch), **trigger conditions** to filter, **retry** policy, **child flows** (in a solution), Dataverse connector with a **service principal** (application user).

**Agents**: integrate Microsoft Foundry agents with Power Platform through MCP servers (including the Dataverse MCP server), connect them to Copilot Studio agents, and give them business context with **Work IQ**.

questions.q: A plug-in must fill in a column of the record before it is written to the database, without a second Update call. At which stage should it be registered?
questions.why: in PreOperation, inside the transaction, you can change the Target entity; the value is saved with the operation, with no extra Update.

questions.q: Which pipeline stage runs outside the database transaction?
questions.why: PreValidation runs before the transaction; an error thrown at that stage cancels the operation with no database rollback.

questions.q: On an Update message, a PostOperation plug-in must compare the old and new status without re-reading the record. What should you configure?

options.t: A pre-image containing the status column
A post-image on the Create message

questions.why: the pre-image provides the values before the operation; with the Target (the new values), you compare with no extra query.

questions.q: What is the maximum execution time of a Dataverse plug-in?
questions.why: plug-ins have a two-minute timeout; running the request asynchronously doesn't give more time.

questions.q: A team wants to expose a "CalculatePrice" business message callable from the Web API, Power Automate and scripts, with typed parameters. What does it create?

options.t: A custom API implemented by a plug-in

questions.why: a custom API defines a new message with its input and output parameters, implemented by a plug-in and available in every API.

questions.q: A plug-in must read a secret from Azure Key Vault without storing any credential. Which approach does Microsoft recommend?

options.t: Put the secret in the step's unsecure configuration
Use the Power Platform managed identity for plug-ins (version 2)
Store the secret in a text environment variable
Call Key Vault with a shared key in the code

questions.why: managed identity lets plug-ins reach Azure resources without managing credentials; version 2 is recommended for all plug-ins.

questions.q: An integration gets HTTP 429 errors from the Dataverse Web API. What should the client do?

options.t: Wait for the duration given by the `Retry-After` header, then retry
Create a new application user for each call

questions.why: the 429 code signals that service protection limits are exceeded; the client must wait for the `Retry-After` duration before retrying.

questions.q: A migration must create 50,000 records in a standard table as efficiently as possible. Which message should you favor?

options.t: One `Create` per record, one after another

questions.why: bulk operation messages (`CreateMultiple`, `UpdateMultiple`…) give the best throughput for large volumes.

questions.q: Two users update the same record through the Web API. How do you prevent the second from silently overwriting the first?

options.t: Send the `If-Match` header with the ETag read
Use a GET method instead of PATCH

questions.why: with `If-Match` and the ETag, the update fails (412) if the record changed since it was read: that's optimistic concurrency.

questions.q: A custom API starts processing that the client doesn't want to wait for with the connection open. It wants to be notified when it ends. Which feature should it use?

options.t: Background operations, with a callback URL or the `OnBackgroundOperationComplete` event
A synchronous plug-in with the timeout raised to 10 minutes

questions.why: background operations run the request asynchronously and signal completion through a callback URL or the `OnBackgroundOperationComplete` event.

questions.q: A reconciliation job takes 40 minutes and coordinates several steps with retries. Where should you implement it?
questions.why: Durable Functions orchestrates long-running, stateful processing, beyond the limits of a plug-in.

questions.q: In a cloud flow, how do you run a branch only when a previous action has failed?

options.t: Use a condition on today's date

questions.why: "Configure run after" defines whether an action runs after the previous one succeeded, failed, timed out or was skipped; combined with Scopes, it forms a try/catch.

questions.q: A flow triggered "When a row is modified" must only run if the status is "Validated". Which approach avoids useless runs?

options.t: A filter at the trigger level ("Filter rows" with an OData expression)
A condition as the first action

questions.why: the Dataverse trigger's "Filter rows" expression is evaluated before the flow starts; the flow only runs if it's true, while a condition as the first action still starts the flow.

questions.q: Several flows must reuse the same discount calculation logic. Which approach is recommended?

options.t: Copy the actions into each flow
A child flow called by the others, in a solution

questions.why: a child flow centralizes the logic; it must be in a solution to be called with the "Run a Child Flow" action.

questions.q: A coding agent must query Dynamics 365 and Power Apps business data, in addition to Microsoft 365 context, through a single MCP server. Which option does the documentation propose?
questions.why: Work IQ MCP exposes Microsoft 365 context and that of supported business apps in a single MCP server; the Dataverse MCP server gives direct access to one environment.

questions.q: A non-Microsoft external service must call Dataverse with no signed-in user (server-to-server). Which configuration should you use?

options.t: An administrator's account with their password
An Entra ID app registration, linked to an application user in Dataverse with a security role

questions.why: server-to-server authentication uses an Entra ID app registration (client credentials flow) associated with an application user that holds the roles.

questions.q: A plug-in must update a related record. How do you get an organization service in the plug-in context?

options.t: By calling the Web API with HttpClient and a hard-coded token

questions.why: the plug-in gets `IOrganizationServiceFactory` from the service provider and creates an organization service for the chosen user.

domaines.fiche:
- **Dataverse events** to the outside: **webhook**, **Azure Service Bus** (queue or topic) or **Azure Event Hubs** service endpoints, registered with the Plug-in Registration Tool. From a plug-in: `IServiceEndpointNotificationService.Execute`.
- **Synchronization**: **change tracking** on the table (only the changes since the last token), **alternate keys** to identify a record by a business value, **Upsert** to create or update in one call.
- **Custom connectors**: from an OpenAPI definition, a Postman collection, an Azure service or GitHub. Authentication: none, basic, API key, OAuth 2.0. **Policy templates** to change runtime behavior (headers, routing…). **Custom code** (C#) to transform requests and responses.

questions.q: Every new order must be sent reliably to a third-party system that will process it later, even if it is temporarily unavailable. Which integration should you choose?

options.t: A synchronous webhook to the third-party system
An Azure Service Bus service endpoint (queue)

questions.why: Azure Service Bus queues the messages; the third-party system consumes them when it's available, with no loss.

questions.q: Every night, a data warehouse must retrieve only the accounts created, changed or deleted since the last sync. Which feature should you use?

options.t: A view sorted by modified date
A scheduled flow that reads the whole table

questions.why: with change tracking enabled, Dataverse returns the changes since a version token, including deletions.

questions.q: An interface receives products identified by their ERP reference, without knowing their Dataverse GUID. How do you create or update in a single call?

options.t: Define an alternate key on the reference and use Upsert

questions.why: the alternate key identifies the record by the reference; Upsert updates it if it exists, otherwise creates it.

questions.q: A custom connector must add a fixed HTTP header to every request without changing the API. Which feature should you use?
questions.why: policy templates change the connector's runtime behavior, for example to add or change a header.

questions.q: An API response must be restructured (renaming fields, flattening an object) before reaching Power Automate, without deploying an intermediate service. Which custom connector option should you use?
questions.why: a connector's custom code (C#) transforms requests and responses directly in the connector.

examens.intro:
AB-410 targets makers of AI-"augmented" business apps: Dataverse data model, model-driven and canvas apps, cloud flows, AI hub prompts and business logic. Microsoft names it as the replacement for PL-200 (Power Platform Functional Consultant), retired on August 31, 2026 ([source](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/skills-hub-blog/the-ai-job-boom-continues-build-the-skills-that-move-business-forward/4494139)).

The skills outline used here is the one announced for December 18, 2026. Since the certification page isn't published yet, the main link points to the study guide.

domaines.nom: Create the foundation for intelligent applications
domaines.fiche:
**Designing the solution**
- Analyze the need, then choose: out-of-the-box, built-in agents, extensibility (code, connectors), environment type (Developer, Sandbox, Production).
- ALM: work in a **solution** (never in the default solution), with a publisher and a prefix, then deploy through **pipelines**.

**Dataverse data model**
- Standard or custom tables; **ownership** chosen at creation (user or team, or organization), not changeable afterwards.
- Typed columns; **relationships** and their behaviors (parental, referential, restrict delete, custom).
- **Prompt column**: an AI column that runs a natural language prompt over other columns of the row and **stores** the result in the table.
- **Row summary**: a Copilot-generated summary from a prompt that picks the columns, shown at the top of the form or from views. An administrator must turn it on in the Power Platform admin center (Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Summary).
- Public views, main forms.
- Security: security roles (privileges × depth), teams, business units, **column security profiles** to protect a sensitive column.

questions.q: A "Contract" table must be assignable to salespeople and shared according to the business unit hierarchy. Which choice should you make when creating the table, knowing it can't be changed later?
questions.why: only user- or team-owned tables have an owner, which enables assignment and business unit security; the ownership type is chosen at creation.

questions.q: Each ticket must get an AI-generated sentiment classification from its description, stored in the row so it can be filtered in views and reports. Which feature should you use?
questions.why: the prompt column runs a prompt over other columns and persistently stores the generated result in the table.

questions.q: Users want to see a Copilot-generated summary of key information at the top of the Account form. The maker wrote the prompt, but nothing shows. What is probably missing?

options.t: An administrator turning on row summaries for the environment, in the Power Platform admin center

questions.why: a Power Platform administrator must turn on "Row summaries" in the environment's Copilot settings; this setting controls summaries on forms and views.

questions.q: Deleting an account must automatically delete its contacts, and assigning the account must also assign its contacts. Which relationship behavior should you configure?
questions.why: the parental behavior cascades actions (delete, assign, share…) from the parent to the related records.

questions.q: The "Salary" column must stay hidden from everyone except the HR team, while the rest of the row is readable by managers. Which mechanism should you use?

options.t: A security role with "User" access level
Hiding the column on the form

questions.why: column-level security restricts reading and writing a specific column to the users and teams of a profile; hiding the column on the form doesn't protect it.

questions.q: A maker creates their tables and apps directly in the default solution. What is the main risk?

options.t: Their components are hard to isolate and deploy cleanly to other environments
The default solution is deleted every month

questions.why: the good practice is to work in a dedicated solution with its own publisher and prefix, so you can export and deploy it.

questions.q: To build without affecting users and be free to reset, which type of environment should a maker use for experiments?
questions.why: Developer and Sandbox environments are made for building and testing; you can reset or copy them without touching production.

questions.q: A salesperson must see all the accounts of their business unit, but only edit their own. How do you configure their security role for the Account table?

options.t: Read at Business Unit level, Write at User level
Read and Write at Organization level
Read at User level, Write at Organization level

questions.why: each privilege has a depth (User, Business Unit, Parent-child, Organization); here read is widened to the unit and write limited to owned records.

domaines.fiche:
**Model-driven apps**
- Forms, views, charts and dashboards; **generative pages** created in natural language.
- Building the app in the designer (navigation, tables, forms and views included).
- Access: share the app with **security roles**; you can also restrict a form to certain roles.

**Canvas apps**
- **Delegation**: when a query can't be delegated, Power Apps only retrieves the first **500** records by default (adjustable up to **10,000**); a blue underline flags the warning.
- Reuse: **named formulas** (`App.Formulas`), **user-defined functions**, **component libraries**.
- Variables: `Set` (global), `UpdateContext` (screen), `Collect` and `ClearCollect` collections.
- Errors: `IfError`, `App.OnError`. Testing and troubleshooting with **Monitor**.
- Accessibility (checker, labels), responsive containers, performance (keep `OnStart` light, prefer named formulas).

questions.q: A gallery filters an 80,000-row Dataverse table with a non-delegable function. How many rows does Power Apps evaluate by default?

options.t: The first 500, a limit adjustable up to 10,000
The first 2,000, with no way to change it

questions.why: a non-delegable query only processes the first records, 500 by default, adjustable up to 10,000; results can therefore be incomplete.

questions.q: A calculated value (the VAT rate for the user's country) is used on several screens. Which recommended approach replaces a long `App.OnStart`?

options.t: A timer that recalculates every second
A collection reloaded on every navigation

questions.why: named formulas are evaluated on demand and stay up to date, which lightens `OnStart` and speeds up startup.

questions.q: Which function creates or changes a variable visible only on the current screen of a canvas app?
questions.why: `UpdateContext` manages context variables, limited to the screen; `Set` creates global variables.

questions.q: A `Patch` call to Dataverse may fail. How do you show the user a clear message instead of a raw error?

options.t: Wrap the call in `IfError` and call `Notify` on failure

questions.why: `IfError` catches the error and lets you run a fallback formula, such as a notification; `App.OnError` handles errors at app level.

questions.q: Several company apps must show the same header with a logo and menu, maintained in one place. What should you create?

options.t: A copy of the screen in each app

questions.why: a component library stores reusable components; the apps that use it receive the updates.

questions.q: A "Financial approval" form must only be offered to financial controllers. How do you configure this in a model-driven app?

options.t: Assign the form to the relevant security roles
Hide it with a business rule

questions.why: you can restrict access to a main form to certain security roles; other users see the fallback form.

questions.q: A canvas app misbehaves only for some users. Which tool lets you follow live the network calls and formulas run during a session?
questions.why: Monitor traces the events of a running app (data calls, formulas, errors) and can follow another user's session.

questions.q: How do you give a team access to a model-driven app?

options.t: Share the app with one or more security roles, and check that these roles have privileges on the tables
Sending the app URL is enough
Add the users as owners of the solution

questions.why: access to a model-driven app goes through the security roles associated with the app; those roles must also grant rights on the data.

domaines.fiche:
**Cloud flows**
- Choose the trigger (Dataverse "When a row is added, modified or deleted" with **Filter rows**, scheduled, instant from an app).
- Choose the connector (standard or premium, already allowed by DLP policies).
- **Approvals**: first to respond, everyone must approve, custom responses, sequential.
- Control: Condition, Switch, Apply to each, Do until; run history and testing with a previous run.

**AI hub (prompts and models)**
- **Prompts** created from a template or from scratch, with **inputs** (text, document, image) and **knowledge** (Dataverse data). You choose the model and the settings.
- Use: in a canvas app or a cloud flow ("Run a prompt" action), and in agents.
- **AI Builder models** (document processing, invoices, classification…) used in apps and flows.

**Business logic**
- **Business rules**: the "Entity" scope applies to all forms and on the server side.
- **Business process flows**: up to **5 tables**, **10** active flows per table, **30 stages** per process.
- **Calculated**, **rollup** (computed by asynchronous system jobs) and **formula** columns (Power Fx, read-only).
- Choose a business rule, formula, flow, plug-in or agent according to the need.

questions.q: A purchase request must be approved by the manager, then by finance management, in that order. Which approval setup fits?

options.t: Two successive approvals in the flow (sequential)
An "Everyone must approve" approval sent to both at the same time

questions.why: to enforce an order, you chain approval actions; the second only starts if the first is approved.

questions.q: The committee must approve a budget: approval is only granted if all three members approve. Which type of approval should you choose?

options.t: Custom responses – Wait for one response
A Do until loop on email

questions.why: "Everyone must approve" waits for every approver's response; a single rejection is enough to reject.

questions.q: For each row of a list of 200 orders, a flow must send a personalized email. Which control should you use?
questions.why: "Apply to each" runs the actions for each item of an array.

questions.q: A flow failed yesterday because of an expired connection. After fixing the connection, how do you rerun that execution with exactly the same trigger data?

options.t: Open the failed run in the run history and resend it with "Resubmit"

questions.why: "Resubmit" reruns a past execution with its original trigger data, once the problem is fixed.

questions.q: A maker creates a prompt in the AI hub that summarizes a complaint. How do you run it automatically when each complaint is created?

options.t: In a cloud flow, with the action that runs the prompt, triggered when the row is created
It's only possible in Copilot Studio

questions.why: a prompt can be used in a cloud flow (and in apps and agents); the Dataverse trigger starts the flow on each creation.

questions.q: A prompt must answer based on the product sheets stored in Dataverse. What should be added to the prompt?
questions.why: you can add Dataverse data as a prompt's knowledge to ground its answers in the organization's data.

questions.q: Supplier invoices arrive as PDFs by email. You must extract the number, date and amount to create a Dataverse row. Which ready-made solution fits?

options.t: The AI Builder invoice processing model in a cloud flow

questions.why: the prebuilt invoice processing model extracts key information from invoices and is used in a flow.

questions.q: A business rule must also apply when data comes in through import or API, not only in forms. Which scope should you choose?
questions.why: the "Entity" scope runs the rule on the server side, whatever the update channel, in addition to forms.

questions.q: How many different tables can a single business process flow link?
questions.why: a business process flow can link up to five tables; a table can have up to 10 active flows, and a process up to 30 stages.

questions.q: The total of open opportunities must show on each account. The value can be a few hours late. Which type of column fits?

options.t: A formula column that queries related rows

questions.why: a rollup column aggregates related rows; it is computed by asynchronous system jobs, hence a possible delay.

questions.q: The "Price incl. tax" column must always equal "Price excl. tax × 1.2", calculated in Power Fx, with no user input. Which type of column?
questions.why: a formula column shows a value calculated by a Power Fx formula; users can't edit it.

questions.q: The sales process must guide the user through the Qualify, Propose and Close stages, with fields to fill at each stage, on the opportunity. What should you configure?
questions.why: a business process flow shows stages and their fields at the top of the form and guides the user through a consistent process.

questions.q: A flow must run different actions depending on five possible values of a "Request type" column. Which control is the most readable?
questions.why: Switch runs a branch based on the value of an expression, without nesting several conditions.

questions.q: A requirement: "when an opportunity exceeds €100,000, make the Justification column required on the form". Which solution is the simplest, with no code?
questions.why: a business rule handles this kind of condition and action (make required, show, set a value) without code.

examens.mots_cles: copilot studio architect architecte agents copilot, copilot studio architect
examens.intro:
**There is no separate "Copilot Studio Architect" certification: AB-100 is the architect exam that covers Copilot Studio** (generative orchestration, topics, MCP, computer use, agent ALM), together with Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Foundry and Dynamics 365. That's why it also appears in the Copilot family. The matching developer level is AB-620.

AB-100 is for architects who design business solutions with agents: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry and Dynamics 365. You plan (strategy, ROI, build or extend), design (agents, orchestration, extensibility) and deploy (testing, monitoring, ALM, responsible AI and security). Microsoft states that AB-100 is not a direct replacement for PL-600 (retired on June 30, 2026), but recommends it as the next step for PL-600 holders ([source](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/skills-hub-blog/the-ai-job-boom-continues-build-the-skills-that-move-business-forward/4494139)).

domaines.fiche:
**Analyzing the need**
- Where an agent adds value: task automation, data analysis, decision support.
- Quality of **grounding data**: accuracy, relevance, freshness, cleanliness, availability. A bad source gives bad answers.

**Strategy**
- Follow the **Cloud Adoption Framework AI adoption** process: start from the use case, then choose the right product (Microsoft AI decision tree).
- Choose the platform: **Microsoft 365 Copilot** (productivity, declarative agents), **Copilot Studio** (low-code, business agents), **Microsoft Foundry** (pro-code, custom models and orchestration).
- **Declarative agent**: your instructions, knowledge and actions, with Copilot's orchestrator and models. **Custom engine agent**: your own orchestrator and models.
- A custom model or a small specialized model only if existing models, well guided and grounded, aren't enough.
- A shared prompt library and prompt engineering rules; an **AI Center of Excellence** for governance and spread.

**Costs and benefits**
- ROI and **total cost of ownership** (licenses, consumption, building, operating, governance).
- **Build, buy or extend**: a ready-made agent or an agent built into Dynamics 365 often costs less than a custom build.
- **Model router** (Microsoft Foundry): a single model name, and each request goes to the best-suited model (Balanced, Quality, Cost modes).

questions.q: A customer wants its salespeople to query their Microsoft 365 emails, meetings and documents in Teams and Outlook, with a few team-specific instructions and a knowledge base. No specific orchestration is needed. Which approach do you recommend?

options.t: A declarative agent for Microsoft 365 Copilot
A custom engine agent with an orchestrator built in Foundry

questions.why: a declarative agent adds instructions, knowledge and actions while reusing Copilot's orchestrator and models; a custom engine agent is justified when you need your own orchestrator or models.

questions.q: When is a custom engine agent preferable to a declarative agent?

options.t: When you only want to add a SharePoint site as knowledge
When you need to control orchestration and choose your own models
When the agent must work in Teams
When you want to reduce development work

questions.why: a custom engine agent brings its own orchestrator and models; it's more work, but more control.

questions.q: An agent often answers with outdated information. The SharePoint site used as knowledge holds three versions of every procedure. What is the first architect action to take?

options.t: Clean up and organize the grounding data (one current version, reliable sources)

questions.why: answer quality depends on grounding data: accuracy, freshness and cleanliness must be addressed before touching the model.

questions.q: An executive asks where to start to adopt AI in a structured way on Azure and Microsoft 365. Which Microsoft framework should you propose?

options.t: The Cloud Adoption Framework AI adoption process
The Microsoft Security Development Lifecycle only

questions.why: the Cloud Adoption Framework offers an AI adoption path and a decision tree that starts from the use case to choose the right product.

questions.q: According to the Microsoft AI decision tree, which product should you recommend to improve individual productivity in Word, Excel and Outlook?
questions.why: for individual productivity in Microsoft 365 apps, the decision tree points to Microsoft 365 Copilot.

questions.q: An application sends very varied requests: simple classifications and complex reasoning. The team wants to cut costs without handling model choice itself. Which Foundry feature should it use?

options.t: A single frontier model for everything

questions.why: the model router assesses each request and sends it to the best-suited model: fast small models for simple requests, frontier models for reasoning.

questions.q: In its default "Balanced" mode, what does the model router do?

options.t: It always picks the cheapest model
It picks the most cost-effective model within a small quality range of the best model for each request
It sends each request to every model and keeps the best answer
It always picks the newest model

questions.why: in Balanced mode, the router picks the most cost-effective model close to the best in quality; the Quality and Cost modes shift this trade-off.

questions.q: In a "build, buy or extend" analysis, Dynamics 365 Customer Service already offers an agent that creates, resolves and closes cases. What is the architect's approach?

options.t: First assess the built-in agent and extend it if needed, before considering a full build
Always build a custom agent to keep control

questions.why: the built-in agent (Case Management Agent) covers creation, resolution, follow-up and closure; extending it generally costs less than a full build.

questions.q: Which item belongs in the total cost of ownership (TCO) of an agent solution?

options.t: Licenses, consumption (messages, tokens), building, operating, monitoring and governance
Only the cost of Dataverse storage

questions.why: total cost of ownership adds up every cost to own, run and maintain the solution over its lifetime, not just the purchase price.

questions.q: A team wants an agent that orchestrates several steps, calls models from different providers and runs custom code, with full pro-code control. Which platform should it favor?
questions.why: Foundry is the pro-code platform to build agents with your own models, orchestration and code; Copilot Studio targets low-code.

questions.q: An organization keeps multiplying agents built by different departments, with no common rules. Which structure do you recommend?

options.t: An AI Center of Excellence that sets standards, governance and reuse
One Power Platform environment per agent, with no common rules
Let each team choose its tools without coordination

questions.why: a center of excellence frames adoption: standards, governance, prompt library, training and reuse.

domaines.fiche:
**Agents and orchestration (Copilot Studio)**
- **Generative orchestration** (default for new agents): the agent picks tools, knowledge, topics and other agents from their **description**. **Classic orchestration**: topics chosen by matching **trigger phrases**.
- System topics, including the **fallback** topic when nothing matches.
- Agent types: conversational, **autonomous** (triggered by events), task agents.
